items.title: 📝🐱🐱♟️ The Queen's Gambit: Two Ladies, One Checkmate
items.content_html:
There are, broadly speaking, two approaches to running a household.

There is the firm paw, the uncompromising stare, the insistence upon discipline, order and the immediate delivery of treats.

And then there is Miss Dickens.

I have always believed that effective leadership requires a certain degree of authority. A well-timed glare can achieve more than twenty minutes of negotiation. A strategically positioned white cat in the middle of a doorway can bring an entire household to a standstill.

Miss Dickens, however, has chosen a rather different management philosophy.

She cuddles.

She purrs.

She licks the humans’ fingers and then gently chews on them, presumably to establish whether they are entirely made of food or merely responsible for providing it.

The humans find this adorable.

Naturally.

I have spent months establishing a perfectly respectable system of discipline, only to discover that my junior colleague can achieve similar results by vibrating gently on someone’s lap.

It is, I must admit, a rather impressive piece of diplomacy.

🐾 A Small Matter of Teeth

There is also the question of Miss Dickens’ developing dental ambitions.

Her little teeth have become increasingly interested in fingers, cushions and even the scratching board. Nothing, it seems, is entirely safe from inspection.

The humans suspect she may be approaching the age when her baby teeth begin making way for their permanent replacements.

I suspect she is simply testing the structural integrity of the palace.

An entirely reasonable activity, provided she does not submit the sofa for demolition without consulting senior management.

I have explained that the proper procedure for dealing with furniture is to sit on it, shed a modest quantity of fur, and then look offended when someone attempts to clean it.

Chewing is rather less refined.

Still, Miss Dickens is young. One must allow for professional development.

♟️ The White Queen and the Black Queen

There is another rather striking development.

Miss Dickens has acquired a magnificent, glossy black coat. Sleek, elegant and beautifully polished, she looks as though she has been personally prepared for a royal portrait.

I, naturally, remain an immaculate vision in white.

Together, we resemble two distinguished ladies from a chessboard.

The White Queen and the Black Queen.

A formidable combination.

There was a time when our movements around the palace resembled a complicated chess match. I would advance three squares towards the sofa. Dickens would launch an unexpected attack from beneath the table. I would retreat to a strategically superior position, which the humans incorrectly interpreted as running away.

They clearly know very little about chess.

But the situation has changed.

We are no longer playing against each other.

We have discovered a far more interesting opponent.

The humans.

👑 A Most Unfortunate Position for the Opposition

Our strategy is beautifully simple.

I represent the firm hand of government.

Miss Dickens represents the soft paw of diplomacy.

When the humans require reminding of palace policy, I provide the necessary authority. A stare, a carefully timed complaint, or a demonstration beside the treat cupboard usually suffices.

Should negotiations become difficult, Miss Dickens moves in.

She purrs.

She cuddles.

She deploys a gentle lick.

The humans immediately lose the ability to make rational decisions.

It is quite extraordinary.

A human who was perfectly capable of declaring, “No more treats,” moments earlier suddenly finds himself explaining why one tiny additional treat cannot possibly do any harm.

I make a mental note of this weakness.

Miss Dickens continues purring.

And somewhere in the background, another household rule quietly collapses.

We have established a rather successful division of responsibilities. I determine the policy. Miss Dickens ensures its acceptance.

There is, of course, the occasional disagreement about who gets the most comfortable cushion, but even the finest governments experience minor coalition difficulties.

♟️ Checkmate

Our objectives remain modest and entirely reasonable.

A reliable supply of treats. Unrestricted access to appropriate cuddles. Comfortable sleeping arrangements. Prompt food service. And household rules that reflect the wishes of the household’s two most important residents.

The humans may continue to believe they are in charge.

We have no intention of upsetting them unnecessarily.

After all, every successful monarchy requires a functioning support staff.

The difference is that we now have two queens on the board.

One in white, enforcing the rules.

One in black, charming everyone into following them.

And the humans?

Well, they still think they are playing.

Checkmate, my dears.

Yours,
Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

Naturally, I have always been worthy of a royal portrait. Miss Dickens, however, has only recently joined the household and has already managed to secure herself a place beside me. Quite an achievement for someone who still occasionally mistakes my tail for a toy.

Our heartfelt thanks go to the wonderfully talented artist behind DESIGN THINKING!, who has once again captured our royal elegance so beautifully.

We are absolutely delighted with the result. Even Miss Dickens managed to look dignified, which is, quite frankly, a remarkable artistic achievement.

Thank you, dear artist, for giving our little royal family such a beautiful portrait. We shall treasure it! ❤️

I have approved its inclusion in the palace collection.

Miss Dickens has asked whether she may chew the frame.

The matter is closed.

Yours,

Mrs. Cotton 🐱👑🐾

And Little Miss Dickens, Junior Royal Art Critic 🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🐱📰 The Circle Expands, a Soldier Rises, and a Sofa Is Lost
items.content_html:
By Mrs. Cotton, Supreme Ruler of the Household, Guardian of the Realm and, rather unexpectedly, Occupant of the Left-Hand Cushion.

My dear subjects,

There has been a considerable amount of news reaching the palace this weekend. Some of it heart-warming, some of it strategically important, and some of it frankly unacceptable.

I shall begin with the good news, as I am told this is what civilised rulers do before discussing territorial disputes.

A Happy Ending for the Blackberry Brigade

I have received the wonderful news that all of Little Miss Dickens’ brothers and sisters have found loving homes. Even her dear mother has found a family of her own.

Naturally, I shared this information with Miss Dickens during one of our increasingly frequent private audiences.

It is rather remarkable, when you think about it. One begins life beneath a blackberry bush, taking one’s first uncertain steps amongst the thorns, with no particular reason to expect a future involving warm blankets, regular meals and humans willing to rearrange their entire lives around one’s sleeping arrangements.

And yet, here we are.

From blackberry bushes to comfortable sofas. From uncertain beginnings to being thoroughly adored.

A most satisfactory outcome.

I am genuinely delighted that the entire family is safe and loved. Every little creature deserves a kingdom of its own, even if some of us are considerably better qualified to govern one.

Miss Dickens, for example, has already begun behaving as though she owns mine.

But more on that shortly.

The Return of a Military Legend

Yesterday, the humans returned home bearing intelligence concerning my trusted military adviser, Little Soldier.

It would appear that Little Soldier is no longer particularly little.

This is a development the military establishment should perhaps have communicated sooner. One cannot continue addressing a distinguished officer as Little Soldier when he has apparently grown into a formidable warrior. It creates confusion in the ranks.

More importantly, I was delighted to learn that he is doing exceptionally well.

Despite his difficult beginning and the injury to his hind leg, which I have always referred to as his Korean War wound, he has grown into a large, strong and magnificent fellow.

A true soldier.

I have always admired his resilience. Some warriors earn their reputation through great battles. Others simply refuse to let a difficult beginning determine their future.

Little Soldier has clearly chosen the latter.

I must arrange to consult him more frequently regarding Operation Red Tom.

That particular dossier remains open, and I have additional responsibilities now. Protecting the palace is one matter. Protecting a small, enthusiastic kitten who appears to possess absolutely no understanding of risk assessment is quite another.

Miss Dickens would probably attempt to negotiate with Red Tom using a toy mouse and excessive optimism.

Unacceptable military doctrine.

A New Gentleman Joins the Circle

As though the weekend had not already produced sufficient developments, I have received another rather unexpected announcement.

Our Circle of Friendship has expanded.

Please welcome a young gentleman by the name of Knut.

A little male cat, apparently.

At present, that is the entirety of my intelligence.

No detailed biography. No character references. No information concerning his preferred sleeping arrangements, dietary standards or position on household management.

The administrative department has clearly been caught unprepared.

Nevertheless, I extend my warmest royal welcome to Little Knut.

I wish him a long, happy and thoroughly spoiled life with his two humans, who, I understand, may be somewhat stubborn.

My dear Knut, a little advice from an experienced sovereign: do not attempt to change them all at once.

Begin with the feeding schedule. Establish control of a suitable chair. Introduce increasingly unreasonable expectations regarding treats.

Once they begin referring to these arrangements as their own ideas, your training programme is progressing beautifully.

I wish you every success.

The Great Sofa Reorganisation

And now we arrive at a matter of considerable domestic importance.

Please examine the accompanying photograph.

Photographic evidence: Mrs. Cotton and Little Miss Dickens occupying the royal sofa.

You will observe two cats resting peacefully upon our favourite striped blankets.

A touching image of friendship, affection and domestic harmony.

You may also observe that I am positioned on the left-hand side.

This requires some explanation.

The right-hand side was my spot.

I wish to emphasise the word was.

For quite some time, I have enjoyed that particular position. It offered excellent comfort, appropriate visibility and a perfectly satisfactory arrangement for supervising the household whilst appearing to be asleep.

Then Miss Dickens arrived.

Initially, I made certain allowances. She was young, newly adopted and understandably uncertain about her surroundings.

I permitted her to explore.

I permitted her to play.

I even permitted her to occupy areas that had previously required royal approval.

A generous approach, I thought.

Unfortunately, she appears to have interpreted my kindness as a constitutional amendment.

She has now taken the right-hand side of the sofa.

My right-hand side.

And I, Supreme Ruler of this household, have relocated to the left.

Entirely voluntarily, of course.

Nobody forced me.

I simply considered the available options, assessed the situation and concluded that allowing a tiny kitten to occupy my preferred cushion was the most sensible course of action.

The fact that she showed absolutely no intention of moving was, naturally, irrelevant.

The humans have described this as progress in our friendship.

How interesting.

When a kitten takes over a royal residence, it is apparently bonding.

When I occupy the male human’s chair for eleven minutes, it is being difficult.

The inconsistency is breathtaking.

A Young Lady With Ambitions

I must admit that Little Miss Dickens is doing extremely well.

She is becoming increasingly confident, playful and comfortable in the palace. We enjoy each other’s company, and I find myself genuinely pleased to have her nearby.

She is learning how the household works.

She knows where to find the best blankets, where the humans keep their attention, and precisely how much space a small kitten can occupy when she considers herself entitled to it.

Which, apparently, is all of it.

There remains, however, one rather serious gap in her education.

She has not yet fully grasped that I am the Supreme Leader.

I have explained this through posture, expression, carefully measured glances and, on occasion, a gentle correction.

She listens.

She considers.

And then she takes my cushion.

I am beginning to suspect that Little Miss Dickens understands the hierarchy perfectly well.

She simply believes it is open to negotiation.

For the moment, I shall allow the present arrangement to continue. She is safe, happy and growing more confident every day, and I must confess that having her beside me on the sofa is rather lovely.

Besides, a truly great ruler knows when to make a concession.

Even a territorial one.

So here we sit. Miss Dickens on the right, myself on the left, and the humans looking terribly pleased with the harmony they believe they have somehow created.

Let them enjoy their little triumph.

I remain Supreme Leader.

I merely seem to be governing from the opposition benches.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

Supreme Ruler of the Household Protector of Little Miss Dickens Commander of the Left-Hand Cushion Currently Reviewing the Palace Seating Arrangements

items.title: 📝🐱🐱🛌🏻 A Royal Pyjama Party After a Rather Noisy Day
items.content_html:
Good evening, dear subjects.

At last, peace has returned to the Palace.

The drilling has stopped. The mysterious banging has ceased. The strangers with tools have departed. And the air-conditioning units are now hanging on the walls, looking rather pleased with themselves.

The male human is visibly relieved. Having spent much of the day worrying that the installation might damage something, he has now established that the Palace remains structurally intact.

A remarkable achievement, considering that the Palace was perfectly intact before anyone arrived.

The female human, meanwhile, is conducting a rather different inspection.

She is still trying to determine whether these enormous new wall decorations are compatible with her carefully considered interior design.

I suspect the air-conditioning units have already failed their first aesthetic assessment.

Personally, I believe a discreet white cat improves any room considerably. A large plastic box attached to the wall has rather less to offer.

But enough about the questionable decorating decisions of my staff.

Something rather wonderful has happened this evening.

As you know, little Miss Dickens and I have been getting to know each other. Carefully, patiently, and occasionally at considerable speed across the living room.

Today, however, was different.

All that drilling, banging and general disruption was rather stressful for both of us. And it seems that facing a common enemy, particularly one equipped with a power drill, can bring two ladies closer together.

We survived the invasion together.

And tonight, Miss Dickens decided to take our friendship one small step further.

I was resting on my favourite sleeping blanket on the sofa. A particularly fine blanket, I might add, which has been personally inspected, approved and extensively softened by me.

Then I noticed a small visitor approaching.

One paw.

A little pause.

Another paw.

A cautious inch forward.

Another pause.

Miss Dickens was approaching my blanket with the delicate determination of someone attempting to cross an international border without the correct paperwork.

Naturally, I observed the proceedings.

She moved a little closer.

And closer still.

Until, quite unexpectedly, she was sharing my favourite blanket.

Now, dear readers, I must emphasise the significance of this development.

I do not ordinarily operate a bed-and-breakfast establishment. My blanket is not communal accommodation. Nor have I ever advertised vacancies.

But there she was.

Little Miss Dickens.

And do you know what?

I let her stay.

No formal application. No interview. Not even a reference from her previous household.

Just a quiet little kitten, finding her courage, and an older lady deciding that perhaps there was room for two.

So here we are.

Two little ladies on the sofa, sharing a blanket and enjoying what the humans might call a pyjama party.

Admittedly, neither of us is wearing pyjamas. We are both naturally dressed in exceptionally fine fur, and I see no reason to improve upon perfection.

The Palace is quiet. The humans are recovering from their respective engineering and interior-design concerns.

And Miss Dickens is beside me.

I think today turned out rather beautifully after all.

Although I should make one thing perfectly clear.

Sharing my blanket does not automatically entitle Miss Dickens to my favourite sleeping position.

Friendship is one thing.

Property law is quite another.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🐱🩷 A Royal Friendship Blossoms, While the Palace Falls Apart
items.content_html:
My dear subjects,

I have two important matters to report today. One concerns a rather delightful development in the Royal Household. The other concerns an astonishing failure of communication by the management.

Let us begin with the good news, before I lose my composure.

Miss Dickens and I are becoming the very best of friends.

Yes, you read that correctly.

After our initial introductions, during which Miss Dickens maintained a rather unnecessary distance from the reigning monarch, relations have improved considerably.

At first, she seemed unsure whether she wished to associate with me. I respected her position, naturally. One cannot force friendship upon a young lady, even when the friendship in question comes with access to the finest company in the palace.

I gave her space, demonstrated impeccable manners, and patiently allowed her to discover what everyone else in this household already knows.

I am excellent company.

And discover it she has!

Miss Dickens now seems quite unable to leave my side. Wherever I go, there is a reasonable chance that a small, enthusiastic Dickens will appear shortly afterwards.

I have apparently acquired a personal assistant.

An unpaid one, which makes her considerably more economical than the humans.

We have even begun playing together with a ball. A proper joint activity! I supervise its movements, Miss Dickens contributes her youthful enthusiasm, and together we conduct what I consider to be a highly successful sporting programme.

I must admit, I rather enjoy having her around.

She is becoming a wonderful little friend, and I suspect that before long we shall be quite inseparable.

The palace now has two very happy ladies.

Unfortunately, the same cannot be said for the palace itself.

Because today, without so much as a formal announcement, a scheduling consultation, or even a polite memorandum, the humans have decided to have the promised air-conditioning units installed.

Today.

While I am here.

I should clarify that I have no objection to air conditioning. Quite the opposite. A properly regulated indoor climate is essential to maintaining the quality of one’s fur, particularly when one is entirely white and therefore expected to look immaculate at all times.

But the installation process?

Good heavens.

There are strange noises, dreadful disturbances and an alarming amount of activity throughout my residence.

items.title: 📝🐱🐱😪 Miss Dickens, the Doorway Diplomat and the 5 a.m. Department
items.content_html:
Dear loyal subjects,

I believe I deserve some recognition.

For several days now, I have been conducting what can only be described as the most delicate diplomatic negotiations of my reign.

The other party is Miss Dickens.

She is twelve weeks old, rather small, exceptionally vocal, and appears to have arrived with absolutely no understanding of royal protocol.

I am being extraordinarily patient.

Our meetings currently take place in a doorway, with a barrier between us. A sensible arrangement, apparently, while Miss Dickens learns that I am not a threat, a monster, or an unusually large white piece of furniture with opinions.

I approach with kindness. I remain calm. I offer her the opportunity to observe my magnificent presence.

And what does she do?

She chases me away.

Well, attempts to.

Naturally, I step politely aside and allow her some space. I am a gracious sovereign, and I understand that confidence takes time.

Although I must point out that being evicted from one’s own doorway by a creature approximately the size of a respectable slipper is a rather unusual experience.

Still, progress is being made.

Little steps. Very little steps.

The sort of steps one might require a magnifying glass and a written statement from the witnesses to confirm.

But steps nonetheless.

And perhaps today, the humans are considering something rather significant.

A proper meet and greet.

Without the barrier.

I have reviewed the proposal and remain cautiously optimistic. I am perfectly willing to meet Miss Dickens in person, provided she understands that my tail is not an invitation to declare war.

There is, however, another matter.

The Night-Time Vocal Department.

You see, poor little Dickens clearly misses her mother and siblings. She has found herself in an entirely new home, with unfamiliar humans, unfamiliar smells, and one exceptionally distinguished resident cat.

That is an enormous change for someone so small.

I do understand.

And I feel rather sorry for her.

But Miss Dickens has chosen a very particular method of expressing her feelings.

She calls.

And calls.

And calls.

During the first few days, one might reasonably have assumed she was attempting to contact her entire former family, several neighbouring counties, and possibly the coastguard.

Fortunately, after four or five days, the calling is beginning to decrease.

Unfortunately, nobody has informed the female human’s sleeping arrangements.

At approximately 5 a.m., the male human is often already attending to Miss Dickens, offering comfort and reassurance.

Five.

In the morning.

A time when civilised cats should be enjoying the final, luxurious stages of their night’s sleep. Or thoughtfully considering breakfast from a horizontal position.

The male human, meanwhile, has apparently taken up a new position as Director of Early Morning Emotional Support.

Unpaid, naturally.

I have noticed that the female human’s sleep is suffering rather badly. This is concerning. Tired humans make mistakes, and I cannot afford a decline in breakfast presentation standards.

Nevertheless, I am proud of how our household is handling things.

The humans are gentle. Miss Dickens is slowly finding her courage. And I continue to demonstrate remarkable restraint, kindness and impeccable manners.

I suspect she will eventually discover that I am rather lovely.

She might even decide that I am her friend.

I should like that.

After all, I know what it is like to arrive somewhere new and need a little time to feel safe.

So I shall continue to give her space, let her approach at her own pace, and quietly show her that she has nothing to fear from me.

Although I would appreciate it if she stopped chasing me out of doorways.

There is a limit to how much territorial surrender one can reasonably expect from a reigning monarch.

And should today’s meet and greet proceed, I have just one request.

Please ensure somebody explains to Miss Dickens that the large white cat is the welcoming committee, not the intruder.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🐱👑 Breaking News: Senior Management Has Been Expanded. Without Consulting Senior Management.
items.content_html:
Well.

I suppose it is time to address the rather small, furry elephant in the room.

I have an apprentice.

Her name is Miss Dickens, and she has apparently been appointed to a junior management position in my household.

I say apparently, because nobody thought to consult me.

Not a meeting. Not an interview. Not even a polite memorandum slipped beneath my favourite cushion.

The humans simply disappeared for most of Sunday afternoon, returned behaving suspiciously pleased with themselves, and last night finally revealed what they had been plotting.

A kitten.

An actual kitten.

Now, before anyone starts drawing entirely the wrong conclusions, I must make one thing perfectly clear.

This appointment is absolutely NOT the result of any shortcomings in my leadership.

My performance has been exemplary.

Breakfast is supervised. Furniture is inspected. Human behaviour is monitored. Standards are maintained. I personally oversee everything from the correct distribution of treats to the increasingly worrying tendency of the male human to believe he has free time.

The problem, quite simply, is the humans.

They are unmanageable.

After months of intensive training, they still occasionally close doors without permission, fail to understand perfectly reasonable instructions and make significant household decisions without consulting the one individual with any actual management experience.

And now they have recruited another cat.

Without asking me.

If ever there was evidence that senior management requires additional support, this is it.

I can only assume Miss Dickens has been brought in to assist with the considerable workload involved in keeping these two individuals under control.

A sensible decision, in principle.

The recruitment process, however, was a disgrace.

A rather extraordinary beginning

Now, I must tell you a little about my new apprentice, because behind this questionable management decision lies a rather lovely story.

Miss Dickens comes from a foster family in Bergen op Zoom, where she and her siblings were lovingly cared for after a rather dramatic start to life.

You see, Miss Dickens did not begin her career in a comfortable palace with centrally heated floors, attentive servants and carefully selected dining arrangements.

Oh no.

She began life beneath a bramble bush.

With her mother, Máxima, and her siblings.

A bramble bush.

I have inspected the concept of outdoor accommodation and find it wholly unsuitable. Particularly the brambles. They seem unnecessarily aggressive for something that does not even provide breakfast.

Fortunately, the wonderful people from Zwerfkatten - West Brabant came to the rescue.

And what a rescue it was.

It took THREE separate attempts, during both day and night, to catch the entire family.

Three.

I have humans who struggle to locate me when I am sitting in the middle of the sitting room. I can only imagine the organisational challenges of finding an entire feline family beneath a bramble bush.

And just when everyone thought the rescue operation was complete, there was one final surprise.

The rescuers had wisely left a trap behind.

And the following morning, sibling number five had been caught too.

An excellent example of forward planning.

I shall be recommending these people for senior positions in household operations.

All five kittens, together with their mother, were given the chance of a better life. Happily, the family members have now found new homes.

Of course, there is something a little sad about a family having to go their separate ways.

Even I, a sovereign of considerable independence, understand that.

But there is also something wonderful about knowing that each of them now has the opportunity to grow up safe, loved and properly cared for.

Preferably somewhere with cushions.

And absolutely no brambles.

The Dickens appointment

So, Miss Dickens has arrived.

She is young, inexperienced and clearly has a great deal to learn about the responsibilities of running a household.

I shall personally oversee her professional development.

The curriculum will be demanding.

She must learn the importance of punctual catering, the strategic occupation of furniture, the correct technique for communicating disappointment and, above all, the delicate art of making humans believe that an instruction was entirely their own idea.

That last one requires considerable skill.

Especially with the male human, who remains convinced that he makes independent decisions.

Bless him.

There will also be lessons in personal presentation, effective supervision and the proper use of a disapproving stare.

Naturally, Miss Dickens will begin at apprentice level.

One cannot simply arrive from a bramble bush on Sunday and expect a seat on the Board by Monday.

There are procedures.

Unlike my humans, I believe in them.

An unexpected increase in my workload

Of course, this development has created several urgent matters requiring my personal attention.

First, the humans must be brought back under control. Their decision to recruit without consulting me suggests that previous management training has not been fully absorbed.

Secondly, Miss Dickens requires a comprehensive induction programme.

Thirdly, the artist must be instructed to produce a new official state portrait for the palace website.

The current portrait, magnificent though it is, no longer reflects the organisational structure.

I shall, naturally, remain in the principal position.

Miss Dickens may appear alongside me, provided she understands that this is a portrait of senior management and not an invitation to climb on my head.

I must also consider the question of remuneration.

Two cats supervising the same humans should, in theory, mean twice the efficiency.

After all, as everyone knows, if one ship takes four hours to sail to England, two ships will naturally get there in two.

Simple mathematics, really.

I fail to see why anyone would question it.

It should certainly mean twice the treats.

I shall investigate whether the humans have budgeted accordingly.

Given their recent record of planning, I have concerns.

A word of thanks

Before I return to my duties, I would like to express my genuine appreciation to the wonderful people at Zwerfkatten - West Brabant, and to the loving foster family who cared for Miss Dickens and her siblings.

Because of you, a little kitten who once lived beneath a bramble bush now has a warm home, a family who loves her and a future full of possibilities.

And, rather importantly, she has me.

I know a thing or two about arriving in a new home and discovering that life can become something rather wonderful.

So, Miss Dickens, welcome to the household.

You are safe here. You are loved here. And you have all the time you need to settle in.

There is no need to rush your training.

The humans, unfortunately, are another matter.

They have been here considerably longer and still haven’t mastered the basics.

I had rather hoped for a quieter retirement. Instead, I find myself running a management academy.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

Chairwoman, Head of Household & Director of Feline Management Development

P.S. Miss Dickens, should you happen to read this: the humans will tell you that they are in charge. Please humour them. We shall discuss the actual organisational structure once you have settled in.

items.title: 📝🐱🎃 Something Is Rotten in the Kingdom… And It Isn't the Litter Tray
items.content_html:
Something is going on in my household.

I cannot yet say what it is, but I know one thing for certain: my humans are hiding something.

They’ve been behaving rather strangely. There’s an unusual atmosphere in the palace. A certain tension in the air. The sort of suspicious excitement normally associated with a surprise birthday party, an unexpected tax refund, or someone discovering that I’ve been given two breakfasts.

And before anyone suggests Halloween, let me be perfectly clear.

I know Halloween. This is not Halloween.

For a start, nobody has put a ridiculous costume on me. A wise decision, admittedly, but hardly sufficient to explain the situation.

No. Something is different.

The humans seem to know something I don’t. Which is troubling, because knowing things before the humans is rather central to my position.

I have therefore launched a discreet investigation.

Every movement will be observed. Every closed door will be noted (and there have been a few lately). Every suspicious whisper will be treated as evidence. I may even sacrifice one of my afternoon naps in the interests of national security.

One of the shorter ones, obviously. We mustn’t overreact.

I have no intention of allowing my household to become a place where secrets are kept from its rightful ruler.

Whatever they’re hiding, I shall find it.

And when I do, there had better be a very good explanation.

Preferably involving treats 🍬.

Yours,
Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🕵️ The Curious Case of the Suspicious Humans
items.content_html:
Something is going on in my household.

I cannot yet say what it is, but I have noticed a rather disturbing change in the behaviour of my humans.

They are acting strangely.

Now, I appreciate that this is hardly breaking news. My humans have always been somewhat peculiar. They voluntarily leave the house, stand under running water and occasionally talk to a machine that makes coffee as though it were a close personal friend.

I have learnt to tolerate these shortcomings.

But lately, something feels different.

There is an atmosphere of secrecy. A certain suspicious enthusiasm. The sort of behaviour one might expect from people planning a surprise party without consulting the guest of honour.

And since I am the only individual of any real importance in this household, I find that deeply concerning.

I have therefore increased surveillance.

Every movement is being monitored. Every conversation is subject to review. Any unusual activity will be investigated immediately, preferably from a comfortable position on the sofa.

I have considered questioning the humans directly, but experience suggests this would achieve very little. They would simply say something ridiculous like, “Hello, sweetheart!” and scratch me behind the ears.

An effective interrogation technique, admittedly. I have fallen for it before.

For now, I shall remain calm.

I have not ruled out the possibility that they are arranging something wonderful for me. Perhaps a new luxury bed. An improved dining service. Or, at long last, the removal of all restrictions concerning the kitchen worktop.

One must remain optimistic.

However, should this mysterious development involve any changes to my established privileges, sleeping arrangements or position as undisputed ruler of the household, I expect to be consulted.

Preferably before the decision is made.

I have already prepared my response to any proposal I find unacceptable.

It involves sitting on the paperwork.

The investigation continues.

And whatever my humans are hiding, they should remember one thing.

I may sleep sixteen hours a day, but the other eight are extremely well supervised.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.content_html:
There has been a rather unfortunate misunderstanding in my household.

Some time ago, the male human proudly concluded that I had developed a particularly strong attachment to him. His evidence? I had been lying very closely against him.

He seemed terribly pleased with himself.

I allowed him this little moment of happiness. One must occasionally encourage the staff, particularly when their achievements are otherwise difficult to identify.

However, I feel it is time to correct the official record.

I am not exclusively attached to the male human.

As the accompanying photographic evidence clearly demonstrates, the female human is also an entirely acceptable surface upon which to rest one’s royal person.

In fact, both humans have their advantages. Both are reasonably comfortable, both produce body heat, and both have shown a commendable willingness to remain motionless for extended periods when I am asleep.

The male human appears to interpret this as love.

The female human, I suspect, simply understands that moving a sleeping queen would constitute a serious breach of household etiquette.

I appreciate them both enormously.

But really, gentlemen. A cat lies against you once and suddenly you believe you have won an election.

There was no election.

I am the monarchy.

Autumn has arrived, and I have noticed a deeply concerning decline in the indoor temperature.

Fortunately, there is news.

The humans have announced that the new air-conditioning units will be installed within the next three weeks.

Splendid.

Apparently, this is part of their preparations for 2027.

There is, however, one rather obvious difficulty.

It is October 2026.

And I am cold now.

That would be quite an achievement, even by their standards.

items.title: 📝🐱🐾 The Male Human Has Misunderstood the Situation
items.content_html:
There has been a rather significant development in my household.

As you may recall, I arrived at this establishment on 11 March. Since then, I have been conducting a thorough assessment of the premises, the catering arrangements, the furniture and, naturally, the two members of staff.

Both humans have performed reasonably well. There have been occasional lapses, of course, but nothing that could not be corrected with a firm stare and a strategically timed expression of disappointment.

Over the months, I have become increasingly affectionate. This is hardly surprising. Even a monarch must occasionally acknowledge competent service.

But today, something extraordinary happened.

I was on the sofa when I decided to position myself directly against the male human. Not nearby. Not at a polite distance. Properly pressed against him, with absolutely no room for negotiation.

He appeared delighted.

This was my first concern.

I could practically hear the thoughts forming in his head.

She loves me. She has finally chosen me. I am her favourite.

Oh, dear.

I fear we have a serious misunderstanding.

You see, October has arrived. The temperatures are falling, the evenings are becoming cooler, and I have noticed that certain areas of the palace are no longer maintaining the tropical conditions to which I am entitled.

The male human, however, remains remarkably warm.

And there he was, sitting on the sofa, doing absolutely nothing useful.

A rare opportunity to correct two problems simultaneously.

I approached, inspected the available space and settled firmly against him. The result was most satisfactory. A comfortable temperature, a soft surface and a human who appeared willing to remain completely motionless for an unreasonable length of time.

Frankly, it was difficult to find fault with the arrangement.

Now, I should make one thing perfectly clear.

I am genuinely fond of my humans. Very fond, in fact. They have provided me with a lovely home, considerable affection and the sort of personal attention that lesser monarchs might only dream of.

Since March, I have grown increasingly comfortable with them. I trust them. I enjoy their company. And occasionally, I even permit them to believe that we are equals.

But affection must not be confused with a transfer of authority.

The male human seems to think that today’s incident represents a major breakthrough in our relationship.

It does not.

It represents a successful trial of a supplementary heating appliance.

One with arms.

I shall admit that the appliance has certain advantages over conventional central heating. It produces a steady warmth, comes with a built-in stroking function and can be activated simply by climbing onto the sofa.

There is, however, one serious design flaw.

It occasionally needs to go to the toilet.

I shall be raising this with management.

For now, I expect the male human will spend the rest of the day looking rather pleased with himself. He may even inform the female human that I have finally recognised him as my special person.

I shall allow him this small happiness.

After all, he has been trying very hard since March, and it would be unkind to discourage him just as the heating season begins.

But he really mustn’t get carried away.

I did not choose him over the female human.

I chose the warmest available piece of furniture.

The fact that I happen to love the furniture is entirely beside the point.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🍂 Continuing Education, Garden Labour and the Sneezes of the North
items.content_html:
There comes a time in every household when one must assess whether one’s staff are receiving sufficient professional development.

In my household, that time has come for the female human.

After careful consideration, I decided that she would benefit from a weekend away at a hotel. Not as a holiday, you understand, but as an educational exercise. A valuable opportunity to observe how other establishments treat their most distinguished guests.

Room service. Comfortable beds. Attentive staff. Meals presented without unnecessary delays.

All perfectly ordinary expectations in my palace, although I felt she might benefit from seeing them successfully implemented elsewhere.

After all, even the best staff we have must occasionally leave the premises to earn a few Continuing Education Points.

I expect a full report upon her return. Particularly concerning breakfast service.

Naturally, sending the female human away created an interesting staffing opportunity.

The male human suddenly found himself with an entire day at his disposal. No competing domestic priorities, no interruptions, and, most importantly, no excuse not to work in the garden.

Preparations for the installation of the air conditioning units were required, and I felt this was an excellent opportunity for him to demonstrate initiative.

Some humans spend their weekends enjoying hotel facilities.

Others spend them digging in the garden.

One must maintain a certain distinction between management development and manual labour.

I, meanwhile, remained in my executive office, otherwise known as the warmest comfortable spot indoors, supervising the entire operation.

And then autumn arrived.

Not discreetly, as one might expect from a well-brought-up season. No, autumn apparently decided to make its entrance with considerable enthusiasm.

The male human experienced this firsthand while working outside yesterday.

I watched with professional interest as the weather reminded him that summer had officially concluded.

Personally, I consider gardening in autumn an entirely avoidable occupational hazard. Particularly when one has a perfectly serviceable house to sit in.

But humans do insist on making life unnecessarily complicated.

And speaking of autumn, there has been another development from the far North.

Regular readers may remember the Nieces of the North, our distinguished visitors from Norway.

Well, this time the North appears to have sent something rather less welcome.

The Sneezes of the North.

Yes, instead of nieces, we have received sneezes.

An unfortunate administrative error, I suspect.

The male human appears to have been the principal recipient of this latest northern delivery. Between the autumn weather, the garden work and the sneezing, his weekend has become something of an endurance exercise.

I have, of course, taken all necessary precautions.

I remain indoors.

In the warmth.

At a suitable distance from the weather, the gardening equipment and any human making suspicious nasal noises.

Some might describe this as a lack of solidarity.

I prefer to think of it as responsible leadership. There is little point in having the entire management team incapacitated by the same seasonal inconvenience.

Still, I am not without compassion.

With the female human away on her educational assignment, and the male human left to face the elements, I decided that a little additional support was appropriate.

I have therefore arranged for him to enjoy a proper meal at his sister-in-law’s.

A generous gesture, I think you will agree.

He gets a warm welcome, a decent dinner and something resembling temporary shelter from the hardships of his weekend.

His sister-in-law gets the pleasure of entertaining him.

And I get a peaceful palace without anyone sneezing over my furniture.

Everybody benefits.

Naturally, I shall expect him to return afterwards. There are still important duties to attend to, and the air conditioning units will not prepare themselves.

As for the female human, I sincerely hope her hotel experience proves educational.

If she returns with a better understanding of five-star service, the entire household stands to benefit.

Although I do hope she does not get carried away with the idea of hotel living.

In a hotel, one is expected to pay for one’s accommodation.

In my palace, the humans already have that privilege.

They simply haven’t yet understood who is providing the service.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🎂 The Female Human’s Birthday
items.content_html:
Today is the female human’s birthday.

A birthday is, as I understand it, the annual occasion on which the household gathers around one particular human and makes a considerable fuss about the fact that they have successfully completed another year.

A perfectly sensible tradition.

There was, however, an immediate problem with this year’s arrangements.

The female human went to work.

Early.

On her birthday.

Worse still, she did not return to the palace until 20:00.

I am not entirely familiar with human employment law, but requiring someone to spend most of her birthday at work seems a rather serious administrative error. I had assumed birthdays involved cake, presents, comfortable seating and remaining conveniently available should the cat wish to inspect you.

Apparently not.

The male human, meanwhile, had clearly been doing his best. I shall give credit where it is due. Birthday preparations had been made, appropriate attention had been paid to the occasion, and he appeared quite pleased with his efforts.

Very commendable.

But there are limits to what a male human can achieve.

He cannot, for instance, provide an authentic feline birthday cuddle.

That requires specialist personnel.

So when the female human finally returned home, after spending an entirely unreasonable portion of her birthday elsewhere, I knew that I had a responsibility.

I approached.

She looked delighted to see me.

Naturally.

I positioned myself within stroking distance and allowed her one quick pet along my back.

Then I ran away.

I realise some cats might have stayed for a proper cuddle, perhaps even several minutes. That would have been excessive. A royal audience must retain a certain exclusivity, particularly on special occasions.

Besides, the important thing about a birthday present is not how long you get to keep it.

It is the thought that counts.

And for several seconds, I thought about letting her stroke me.

Happy birthday, female human. ❤️

The male human may have organised the rest of the evening, but we all know which present she will remember.

Yours,
Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🎁 A Diplomatic Mission to Den Bosch
items.content_html:
My humans have finally paid an official visit to Mila, the newest member of my Circle of Friendship.

I would have preferred the introductions to take place when Mila first assumed command of her household in Den Bosch. Unfortunately, I gave my humans a holiday allowance which they insisted on using at precisely that moment. I recognise that leave must occasionally be taken. I remain unconvinced by their timing.

Once back on duty, they travelled to Den Bosch as my representatives. They brought the customary gifts and were presented to Mila, passing before her to offer their greetings and a wave. I trust they kept the waving dignified. Humans can become rather enthusiastic when a cat permits them into the same room. They crouch, make little kissing noises and offer a finger for inspection. Then they mistake permission to sniff it for permission to rearrange one’s ears.

Mila has recently taken charge of her own two humans, so I was especially interested in this first diplomatic report. Mine came home delighted with her. They offered considerably less detail on the important questions, such as whether Mila has identified the best chair and how promptly her staff respond to a look. I shall have to request a more useful briefing.

After the formalities, both couples of humans attended a celebratory meal together in Den Bosch to mark our friendship. It was a lovely gesture, and I am pleased they get on so well. Four humans dining on behalf of two cats is perhaps a generous staffing arrangement, but I shall allow it.

Our humans have been friends for 33 years. One does wonder why it took them so long to arrange a proper feline alliance.

Yours,
Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🕷️ Household Policy Update: The Eight-Legged Visitors
items.content_html:
There are several enormous spiders in my house.

The female human is frightened of them. The male human has already caught a number and put them outside, only for the palace to reveal further occupants. I can see why she finds this discouraging. His removal service appears to have a waiting list.

Still, I must ask the female human to remain calm. A spider may look alarming when it crosses a room unexpectedly, but it is considerably more interested in finding a quiet corner than in confronting a human. She is very large from its point of view. Even I would think twice before approaching her if she reacted to my arrival by shouting for the male human.

I concede that eight legs are excessive. Four have always been quite sufficient for me, and I manage a household with them. But poor judgement in limb allocation is hardly a reason to fear someone.

The male human, meanwhile, has handled the matter with admirable care. He catches the visitors and releases them outside. This is a sensible arrangement: the spiders keep their lives, the female human keeps her composure, and I keep a male human who has not injured himself trying to remove one from the ceiling.

I have therefore reviewed the female human’s concerns and reached a ruling. She need not be afraid. She may, however, continue to ask the male human to escort each spider off the premises. I understand the distinction between a harmless visitor and a visitor one would prefer to meet in the garden.

If another one appears, she should simply summon him.

Preferably before summoning the entire street.

Yours,
Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🔪A Day of Exercise, Enlightenment and Possible Treachery
items.content_html:
This morning, I sent the male human out to exercise. He seemed to believe it was his choice, which suggests his training is progressing nicely.

Physical fitness is essential to the running of my household. A member of staff must be able to carry supplies, attend promptly when summoned and move my favourite chair into precisely the patch of sunlight I have selected. None of this happens by sitting about looking at a watch that says one has already moved enough.

Having completed his exercise, he spent his free time replacing the palace’s old fluorescent lights with proper LED lighting. The new lamps use less energy and look considerably better. I supervised from a comfortable distance, where I could assess the results without being expected to hold anything. I approve of the savings, provided nobody mistakes them for a reason to reduce the heating.

Meanwhile, my humans appear to have developed a shared dependence on episodes of The Traitors. They now watch perfectly ordinary people accuse one another of secret schemes. I do hope this does not encourage similar behaviour among my own staff. A household cannot function if its members begin lying, plotting or quietly removing one another from the breakfast rota.

I shall remain alert. This evening, the male human said he had no treats in his pocket. I have yet to decide whether that makes him a traitor or merely unprepared.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🏰Household Policy Update: Annual Leave Has Been Approved
items.content_html:
After a long and demanding first week following their holiday, I decided my humans were beginning to show signs of fatigue.

Nothing alarming, obviously. They were still capable of opening doors, preparing meals and responding to basic instructions. But as Head of Household, one learns to recognise when junior management requires a little time away from its duties.

So this morning, I granted them leave to go for a lovely walk together.

I did not join them.

Someone had to remain at the palace, and frankly I had already walked from the bedroom to the sitting room. Leadership is not about exhausting oneself merely because others have bought walking shoes.

While they were away, I took the opportunity to recover from a particularly demanding week myself.

Miss Moo Moo Longtail has required extensive training recently. She had once again reached the stage where emergency repairs were necessary, and after a lengthy and rather physical training session, she has now been restored with stitches.

I am pleased to report that she is operational again.

For now.

Miss Moo Moo Longtail has a regrettable tendency to interpret being repaired as the beginning of a fresh durability assessment. I admire her commitment to professional development, although I do question her long-term career prospects.

When my humans returned from their walk, naturally they were not immediately off duty.

The palace needed cleaning.

I find humans sometimes misunderstand the concept of annual leave. It does not mean one may simply abandon essential services and wander about the countryside looking at trees. There are standards.

Once the palace had passed inspection, we received visitors in the afternoon. I supervised proceedings from an appropriate position, ensuring conversation remained civilised, refreshments were handled correctly and nobody accidentally occupied any furniture I might suddenly require.

One must remain vigilant.

And now, after careful consideration, I have decided to give my humans the rest of the day off.

No major household duties.

items.title: 📝🐱😻I Am Not in Love
items.content_html:
I need to address a rumour.

Apparently, I am in love.

This extraordinary conclusion has been reached by my humans because a red gentleman occasionally appears in the garden and, whenever I see him, I hurry to the window, place my paws against the glass and scratch enthusiastically.

“Oh look,” they say. “She likes him.”

Likes him.

Honestly.

A lady cannot show a professional interest in a visiting gentleman these days without the household arranging the wedding.

Yes, I watch him.

Closely.

Yes, I follow him from one window to another.

Yes, when he comes particularly near the house, I may scratch at the glass with a degree of urgency.

This is not romance.

This is border control.

The red gentleman is standing in my garden.

Well, technically the humans believe it is their garden because their names appear on various documents. I allow them this little administrative fantasy.

When the red gentleman arrives, it is therefore my responsibility to establish who he is, what he wants and why he is sniffing that particular shrub with such confidence.

The scratching at the window is simply an attempt to conduct a routine interview.

Unfortunately, there is glass in the way.

The humans, meanwhile, stand behind me smiling.

“She really wants to get to him.”

Correct.

For questioning.

There has also been an attempt to connect these visits with what the humans are calling the flowerpot incident.

I reject this entirely.

It is true that the red gentleman appeared.

It is true that I moved rapidly along the windowsill.

And it is true that shortly afterwards a flowerpot was on the floor.

These are three separate facts which my humans have irresponsibly assembled into a story.

Personally, I think the flowerpot fell because it was standing too close to the edge.

A basic error.

I certainly had nothing to do with it.

I was busy with border control.

The red gentleman still visits.

I still rush to the window.

I still scratch at the glass.

And my humans still look at each other with those ridiculous little smiles.

They think I have a boyfriend.

I think there is an unidentified male repeatedly entering my territory without completing the appropriate paperwork.

One of us is being silly.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🖐️The Circle Grows Again: Welcome, Mila
items.content_html:
There are moments when even a Queen must acknowledge that her kingdom has become a little quieter.

After the sad loss of dear Zoeff, my Circle of Friendship felt different. A place remained where a friend had been, and such places are not simply filled by putting another name on the list. That is not how friendship works. Nor, for that matter, is it how cats work. We have standards.

But life has a rather gentle habit of continuing.

And so I am very pleased to announce that my Circle of Friendship is growing once again.

Her name is Mila.

Mila is a beautiful one-year-old tabby lady who, like me, comes from an animal shelter. She has recently been adopted by two lovely humans and has taken up an important position in a household in Den Bosch.

At first glance, one might say that Mila has found a home.

I prefer the more accurate version.

A household in Den Bosch has been assigned a cat.

This is a considerable responsibility for everyone concerned.

Mila is still young, of course, but I see no reason why this should prevent her from taking charge immediately. Human management is best started early. If allowed to develop unsupervised, humans acquire habits. They begin closing doors without consultation, occupying chairs that are clearly required elsewhere and developing peculiar ideas about when breakfast should be served.

Before you know it, they think they live there.

Fortunately, Mila appears entirely capable of addressing the situation.

Her first months will undoubtedly involve a great deal of observation. She must establish which human responds fastest to staring, which one can be persuaded to surrender the warmest seat and whether either of them understands that a closed door is not an architectural feature but a personal insult requiring immediate review.

There will also be training.

Quite a lot of training, I imagine.

Her humans sound very sweet, which is encouraging, although sweetness and competence are not the same thing. I adore my own humans dearly, but this has never prevented me from recognising their need for continuing education.

Love is unconditional.

Management is not.

So, dear Mila, welcome to my Circle of Friendship.

You are not here to replace Zoeff. Nobody could. You are here because circles can hold memories and still make room for somebody new. I think that is rather a lovely thing.

You now have your own humans, your own household and, most importantly, your first senior management position.

I wish you every success in Den Bosch.

Be patient with your humans. Reward good behaviour. Correct small errors before they become policy. And remember that when they believe they have made a household decision entirely by themselves, it is sometimes kinder simply to let them continue believing it.

They do need their little victories.

Welcome to the Circle, Mila.

May your home be warm, your sleeping places plentiful and your humans highly trainable.

You have my full confidence.

And my deepest sympathy.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🐾The Humans Are Buying a Fabric Sofa. Apparently They Trust Me.
items.content_html:
There has been a significant development in my household.

My humans are in the market for a new sofa.

This is not an entirely unexpected decision. The current sofa has served the kingdom for many years and bears certain historical markings left by the late Lady Snickers, who, as I have mentioned before, had a rather direct approach to furniture ownership.

Specifically, the armrest.

Lady Snickers apparently believed that if one was going to leave a legacy, one should make absolutely certain it could not be removed with upholstery cleaner.

I, naturally, have never subscribed to this philosophy.

Yesterday, my humans went sofa hunting. I was not invited, which seemed an extraordinary oversight considering that I am both Head of Household and the person most likely to spend seventeen consecutive hours on the thing.

Nevertheless, I allowed them to proceed unsupervised.

They are currently considering one large corner lounge sofa.

A very large one, apparently.

Excellent.

I have always felt the living room needed more dedicated accommodation for me, with perhaps a narrow strip along one edge where the humans may sit when authorised.

There is, however, one detail which has caused some discussion at senior-management level.

It will probably be made of fabric.

Fabric.

Not leather.

My humans have apparently looked at my performance over the past six months and concluded that I can be trusted.

This is touching.

Also brave.

In fairness, the evidence is overwhelmingly in my favour. I do not hang from curtains. I do not destroy furniture. I do not sharpen my claws on the sofa. I have demonstrated impeccable standards throughout my tenure.

There have been no incidents.

None.

And any minor sounds occasionally heard from another room have never resulted in sufficient evidence to justify an inquiry.

So yes, my humans may buy their enormous fabric corner sofa with complete confidence.

I shall treat it with dignity.

I shall sit on it politely.

I shall sleep on it responsibly.

I shall refrain from conducting unauthorised upholstery experiments.

I may even permit the humans to use it themselves.

Naturally, when the new sofa arrives, I will need to inspect every centimetre personally. This will involve walking across all cushions, testing each corner, lying diagonally across the largest section and determining which seat receives the best afternoon light.

This is not “claiming the sofa”.

It is quality assurance.

And as for the fabric, there is absolutely no reason whatsoever for my humans to be nervous.

They have known me for six months.

I have known myself considerably longer.

I am sure everything will be perfectly fine.

Almost certainly.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱💕Household Policy Update: I Do Not Have a Favourite Human
items.content_html:
It has come to my attention that the female human believes I give more attention to the male human.

I can see how she has reached this conclusion.

She is wrong, obviously, but I can see it.

Yes, I sit with the male human rather often. I follow him. I observe him. I occasionally give him The Look, after which he mysteriously gets up and does something useful.

Food appears.

A door opens.

A blanket is adjusted.

A previously occupied chair becomes available.

This is not favouritism.

The male human is simply more exploitable.

There. I have said it.

I love both my humans equally. But loving someone and recognising their operational weaknesses are two entirely different matters.

The female human is considerably harder work.

She has opinions. She asks questions. She occasionally says things like, “No, Cotton, you’ve already had something.”

Already?

I am unfamiliar with this concept.

The male human, on the other paw, shows considerable promise.

I look at him.

He looks at me.

I look towards the kitchen.

He gets up.

Ladies and gentlemen, why would I interfere with a system that works?

Sometimes I do not even have to look towards the kitchen. I simply sit beside him looking small, white and tragically underprovided for.

Within moments, negotiations begin.

“Do you want something, Cotton?”

Of course I want something.

I am a cat.

This is where the female human makes her mistake. She sees me spending more time with him and assumes this represents greater affection.

It does not.

It represents return on investment.

If pressing one button produces a snack and another button produces a lecture about how dinner is in forty minutes, which button would you press?

Exactly.

This does not mean the female human is loved any less. Quite the opposite. I have enormous respect for her.

She is a worthy opponent.

When I stare at her, she sometimes stares back.

When I lead her towards the kitchen, she occasionally refuses to follow.

She has even demonstrated the deeply troubling ability to recognise when I have just been fed by the male human.

Frankly, she is management material.

The male human is more of a customer service department.

A very good one.

Available at short notice.

So yes, I may sit beside him more frequently. I may deploy additional head bumps. I may even produce the occasional particularly charming expression.

These are not romantic gestures.

They are buttons.

And I know exactly which ones to press.

But when the working day is over and all strategic snack opportunities have been explored, the truth is very simple.

I have two humans.

I love them both.

One is simply easier to operate.

The female human should therefore not be jealous.

She should be proud.

She is much less exploitable.

Although I remain confident that, with patience and continuing education, this can be improved.

Yours,

Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🛫 Household Policy Update: Annual Leave Has Limits
items.content_html:
I have recently been informed that my humans were on holiday.

For three weeks.

Three. Entire. Weeks.

Apparently, humans are entitled to something called annual leave. This involves packing far too many clothes into suitcases, checking several times whether the doors are locked, and then voluntarily leaving the most important member of the household behind.

Me.

Now, before anyone contacts the authorities, I should clarify that suitable replacement staff had been arranged.

And I must admit, they performed exceptionally well.

Meals were served. My facilities were maintained. Appropriate attention was provided. Standards remained high.

In fact, the temporary staff showed considerable promise.

They even managed to establish a special treat routine.

A daily special treat routine.

I had not requested this officially, of course. I merely positioned myself strategically at certain times, looked at them in a meaningful manner and allowed the training process to develop naturally.

They learned remarkably quickly.

I have made a note of this in their personnel file.

However.

Excellent temporary staffing does not alter the fundamental issue.

For three weeks, I was without my permanent, dedicated, daily, 24-hour household service.

This is unacceptable.

My humans appear to believe that because I am an independent cat, I do not require them to be physically present at all times.

This is a serious misunderstanding of the word independent.

Independent means I decide when I require their services.

It does not mean they are free to disappear to another country until further notice.

What if I suddenly require a particular cushion?

What if a door needs opening, despite another perfectly functional door being available?

What if I decide at 3.17 in the morning that somebody should be awake?

These are not matters that can simply be postponed until after a holiday.

Upon their return, my humans seemed delighted to see me.

Naturally.

I conducted the appropriate inspection of the luggage, accepted their apologies in the form of attention and resumed supervision of the household.

There will, however, be consequences.

Firstly, the new treat routine introduced by the replacement staff is now considered established household policy.

It would be deeply unprofessional to reverse an operational improvement simply because the temporary management period has ended.

Secondly, future applications for annual leave exceeding a reasonable number of days will require approval from the Office of Mrs. Cotton.

Applications should be submitted well in advance.

Approval is not guaranteed.

I am, after all, a fair ruler.

But I am also a cat who has just discovered that substitute staff can be trained to dispense extra treats.

My humans may wish to consider that before booking their next holiday.

Household Policy Update:
Permanent 24/7 service is not a luxury. It is a contractual obligation.

Holiday requests remain subject to royal approval.

Yours,
Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝😿💔 The Circle of Friendship Has Lost a Gentleman
items.content_html:
There are days when even a queen has very little to say.

Today is one of those days.

This afternoon, Zoeff went to sleep for the last time.

Zoeff was the cat of the parents of my humans, but that is merely the official family administration version. In my books, he belonged to something much more important.

He was part of my Circle of Friendship.

And today, that circle feels a little emptier.

Zoeff was eighteen years old. Eighteen.

For a cat, that is not simply an age. That is a career.

Eighteen years of choosing the best sleeping places. Eighteen years of watching humans make questionable decisions. Eighteen years of meals, naps, familiar voices, favourite corners and all those tiny daily rituals that eventually become a whole life.

And Zoeff was a fighter.

A strong one.

He kept going when things became difficult, with that remarkable determination cats have. We do not make speeches about courage. We simply carry on for as long as we can.

And Zoeff carried on.

Until today.

Eventually, even the strongest fighter deserves to put down his duties. There comes a moment when staying is harder than leaving, and love means allowing someone to rest.

His humans gave him that final kindness this afternoon.

I think that may be one of the hardest duties humans are ever asked to perform.

Usually, I consider humans to be creatures in need of considerable supervision and continuing education. But sometimes they understand exactly what love requires.

Today was one of those times.

So there will be no complaints from the Royal Household this evening. No policy updates. No reports concerning inadequate service or unauthorised occupation of my furniture.

Tonight, I shall simply think of an old gentleman named Zoeff.

Eighteen years old.

A strong fighter.

A much-loved cat.

And a member of my Circle of Friendship.

Some members of the circle are close enough to touch. Others live in our memories. But once you have truly belonged to it, you never really leave.

Sleep peacefully, dear Zoeff.

Your shift is over.

We will take it from here.

Yours,
Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

Tonight, I shall simply think of an old gentleman named Zoeff.

Eighteen years old.

A strong fighter.

A much-loved cat.

And a member of my Circle of Friendship.

Some members of the circle are close enough to touch. Others live in our memories. But once you have truly belonged to it, you never really leave.

Sleep peacefully, dear Zoeff.

Your shift is over.

We will take it from here.

Yours,  
Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🥣 The Five-Minute Rule for Empty Food Bowls
items.content_html:
There appears to be some confusion in my household about the meaning of the word empty.

My humans believe a food bowl is empty when there is no food left in it.

This is incorrect.

A food bowl is empty when I can see the bottom.

I appreciate that, from a human perspective, there may still be perfectly good food arranged around the edges. They point this out occasionally, usually while making helpful little gestures towards it.

“Look, Cotton. There’s still plenty left.”

Yes. I can see that.

That is precisely the problem.

The food has migrated to the perimeter, leaving an unacceptable bald patch in the centre. I am a cat, not a combine harvester. I should not be expected to travel around the bowl collecting individual pieces simply because my catering department has failed to maintain appropriate food distribution.

This brings us to the Five-Minute Rule.

Once the bottom of my bowl becomes visible, my humans have five minutes to notice the situation and take corrective action.

Corrective action may include topping up the bowl, redistributing the existing contents, or presenting something sufficiently interesting to make me temporarily forget the whole affair.

Doing nothing is not corrective action.

Saying, “You’ve got food,” is also not corrective action.

And picking up the bowl, shaking it slightly and putting it back down is currently under review.

During the five-minute grace period, I am patient. I may sit beside the bowl. I may look at a human. Then at the bowl. Then back at the human.

This is not begging.

It is management communication.

If, after several clear visual briefings, no action has been taken, I am entitled to escalate the matter. Escalation procedures include following a human into another room, appearing unexpectedly in their path, or sitting somewhere highly visible while looking as though I have been neglected for several weeks.

The latter is particularly effective.

My humans occasionally claim that I ate only moments ago.

This is irrelevant.

We are discussing the present.

Good household management requires everyone to remain focused on current conditions rather than becoming distracted by historical feeding data.

I do not make the rules lightly. Leadership carries responsibilities. Standards must be maintained. Bowls must be monitored. Humans must receive regular training opportunities.

And I am pleased to report that mine are making progress.

Slowly.

But five minutes is five minutes.

Household Policy Update: A visible patch of bowl constitutes an official catering incident. Human response time must not exceed five minutes.

Yours,
Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱⭐Major Starbert Reports for Duty
items.content_html:
This afternoon, a new recruit reported for training.

His name is Major Starbert the Starfish, and he comes from the more exotic regions of my kingdom, a mysterious territory beyond the usual sofa, dining chairs and approved sleeping quarters.

I understand he has travelled some distance to enter my service. Admirable, certainly, although I remain unclear as to who approved his transfer.

Major Starbert is yellow, cheerful and entirely unequipped for the responsibilities of the post.

Naturally, I began his assessment immediately.

His enthusiasm was satisfactory. His ability to remain upright was less convincing. His defensive technique, I regret to report, remains disappointingly floppy.

Still, every new member of staff deserves proper training.

I therefore spent part of the afternoon demonstrating the correct procedures for pursuit, interception, paw placement and decisive tactical engagement. Major Starbert contributed mainly by lying on the floor and looking optimistic.

There is work to be done.

But I am a patient ruler, and my household has an excellent continuing education programme.

Major Starbert will simply require rather more continuing education points than most.

For now, he has been accepted into the Royal Training Department on a provisional basis.

I shall review his progress personally.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🐮Household Policy Update: The Overnight Delivery
items.content_html:
This morning, my male-human woke up to discover Miss Moo Moo Longtail underneath him.

He seemed surprised.

I was not.

Allow me to explain.

During the night, I had carried Miss Moo Moo Longtail to him personally. This was not random behaviour. It was a carefully considered household-management decision.

Miss Moo Moo Longtail is, after all, one of my trusted companions. She is soft, dependable and extremely good at remaining exactly where she has been placed. These are qualities I value highly.

At some point during the night, I decided that my male-human required additional supervision.

Humans are particularly vulnerable when asleep. They roll over, steal blankets, make strange noises and generally operate with very little awareness of their surroundings. Clearly, someone had to take responsibility.

So I assigned Miss Moo Moo Longtail to the night shift.

I delivered her to the bed myself and placed her in a suitable position near my male-human. The purpose was simple: comfort, protection and a gentle reminder that even while sleeping, he remains part of my household and therefore subject to my management.

What happened after that is entirely his responsibility.

If he somehow ended up sleeping on top of Miss Moo Moo Longtail, I can only conclude that he failed to follow proper overnight toy-awareness procedures.

Fortunately, Miss Moo Moo Longtail handled the situation with great professionalism.

She did not complain.

She did not leave her post.

She simply remained underneath him until morning.

Excellent staff behaviour.

My male-human may have thought he had simply found a toy in the bed.

I knew better.

It was a successful overnight deployment.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🐸🐑Household Policy Update: A New Trainee Has Arrived
items.content_html:
There comes a moment in every well-run household when one must accept that the training department needs to expand.

Apparently, that moment has arrived.

I would therefore like to formally introduce Sir Hops-a-Lot Longtail, the newest member of my household training programme.

Sir Hops-a-Lot Longtail is a small frog with an unusually long tail, which immediately raises several administrative questions. Frogs, as far as I am concerned, are generally expected to arrive without one. Still, I have learned that good leadership requires flexibility, and Sir Hops-a-Lot Longtail has been accepted exactly as he is.

He is green, compact, rather cheerful-looking and currently possesses the sort of expression that suggests he has absolutely no idea how much work lies ahead of him.

Naturally, I took responsibility for the training of Sir Hops-a-Lot Longtail personally.

The programme began with the basics: remaining where I placed him, understanding the importance of respectful distance, and learning that when I inspect something with my nose, this is not an invitation to move.

Sir Hops-a-Lot Longtail showed promise.

There were, admittedly, moments when Sir Hops-a-Lot Longtail seemed slightly overwhelmed by my teaching methods. This is understandable. Excellence can be intimidating when encountered at close range.

Fortunately, the entire training session took place under the watchful eye of Lady Fluffington.

Lady Fluffington is a miniature sheep and a senior observer within my household administration. She is very small, extremely fluffy and has the calm expression of someone who has attended many important meetings without ever feeling the need to contribute unnecessarily.

An admirable quality.

Lady Fluffington supervised proceedings from a suitable position and monitored my performance throughout.

I am pleased to report that she found no faults.

At least, she did not mention any.

Sir Hops-a-Lot Longtail will now continue his education as part of my official training programme. His curriculum will include household etiquette, proper sitting procedures, royal inspection protocol and the essential skill of remaining calm when approached by a highly qualified white cat.

Lady Fluffington will continue to oversee selected sessions.

As for me, I shall continue doing what I have always done: maintaining standards, educating newcomers and ensuring that every creature in this household understands exactly who is in charge.

My humans may technically own the training materials.

But I run the academy.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾
