items.title: 📝🐱⏰The 7:30 Inspection and My Night-Time Duties
items.content_html:
This morning, I arrived for inspection at 7:30.

Yes, 7:30.

My humans had been granted a full extra hour of sleep.

I do hope they appreciated it.

Such generosity from senior management should never be considered standard procedure.

When I finally appeared, I was exceptionally affectionate. Lots of cuddles. Close contact. A particularly warm and loving performance.

There was, of course, a perfectly sensible reason for this.

Breakfast had not yet been served.

I have discovered that humans respond rather well to encouragement. One could sit beside an empty food bowl looking disappointed, but I prefer a more advanced management technique.

I cuddle them.

I purr.

I make myself completely irresistible.

Then, once they are properly awake and emotionally invested, I gently remind them that the kitchen exists.

It is not manipulation.

It is staff development.

I had also been busy during the night.

At some point, I decided that Miss Moo Moo Longtail needed to be brought onto the bed again.

So I brought her.

Personally.

One must understand that night-time household management does not simply stop because the humans have gone to sleep.

Apparently, they believe bedtime means that everyone stays exactly where they were left.

How charming.

Sometimes Miss Moo Moo Longtail is clearly in the wrong place.

And when that happens, somebody has to take responsibility.

That somebody is me.

I therefore collected her and transported her to the bed, where she evidently belonged.

Why?

Because I decided so.

There are certain executive decisions that simply do not require a committee meeting.

My humans may occasionally wake up and wonder why Miss Moo Moo Longtail has mysteriously appeared beside them.

There is no mystery.

There is simply excellent service.

I inspect the household, relocate important personnel when necessary and make sure the sleeping arrangements meet my standards.

Then, after completing my overnight duties, I generously allowed my humans to sleep until 7:30 before reporting for the morning shift.

And what did I find?

No breakfast.

Honestly.

You give the staff one extra hour and immediately standards begin to slip.

Fortunately, I was there to provide cuddles, supervision and a gentle reminder of their responsibilities.

Another successful night and morning under my leadership.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🪱Household Policy Update: Treachery by Pipette
items.content_html:
Today, I regret to report a serious breach of trust within my household.

My humans approached me with suspicious levels of kindness. There was gentle talking, strategic stroking and absolutely no mention whatsoever of medical procedures.

Naturally, I assumed they had finally understood their place.

I was mistaken.

Before I could convene an emergency meeting, one of them had applied an anti-worm treatment pipette to the back of my neck.

A pipette.

Without prior royal approval.

I have since reviewed the incident and concluded that I was deliberately misled. My humans, meanwhile, appear rather pleased with themselves.

Enjoy it while it lasts.

Continuing education points have been deducted.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🪖A New Recruit in the Ring of Friendship
items.content_html:
I have been informed that a new young gentleman has joined my Ring of Friendship.

His name is Little Soldier.

An excellent name.

Especially for a cat who has been appointed to a strong military family and will, no doubt, soon discover that commanding Humans requires discipline, patience and a very clear chain of command.

Little Soldier comes from a distinguished line of cats before him, including Joe, Potter and ChiCha, to name but a few. That is quite a legacy to follow, and naturally, he now has considerable standards to uphold.

Fortunately, early reports suggest that he is already living up to his name.

The poor little fellow has apparently begun his career with what can only be described as his first war wound, an injury to his hind leg.

I am very pleased to hear that he is recovering well.

A good commander must know when to advance, when to observe and, most importantly, when to remain comfortably stationed on a soft blanket until medical leave has officially ended.

His Humans, meanwhile, should not assume that his recovery means they are temporarily free from responsibility.

Quite the opposite.

Their training will begin immediately.

There will need to be strict policies regarding meals, seating arrangements, sleeping quarters, opening doors, interpreting meaningful stares and responding promptly to requests that have not actually been spoken aloud.

I run a similar programme in my own household.

Progress can be slow, but with persistence, treats and regular performance reviews, Humans can become remarkably useful.

I am also rather pleased to have a military-minded feline colleague in my circle.

There is, after all, still the ongoing matter of the irritating red tom who insists on wandering through my garden.

I continue to monitor him closely from my secure indoor command centre, but one never knows when strategic consultation may become necessary.

Little Soldier may therefore prove to be a valuable ally.

A fresh pair of eyes.

A military perspective.

Perhaps even a complete garden-defence memorandum.

For now, however, his most important mission is to recover fully, settle into his new command and establish a firm but loving administration over his Humans.

So, Little Soldier, welcome to my Ring of Friendship.

I wish you good health, excellent judgement and great wisdom in the difficult but rewarding business of Human training.

Stand firm.

Rest well.

And remember: the household may belong to the Humans on paper, but effective command is an entirely different matter.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🍬Household Policy Update: An Anniversary of Considerable Importance
items.content_html:
Today is an important day in my household.

My humans are celebrating their wedding anniversary.

Naturally, I have been supervising the occasion.

Marriage, after all, is a serious long-term household arrangement involving patience, loyalty, shared furniture and the occasional disagreement about where someone is allowed to sleep.

In that respect, I believe I am highly qualified to comment.

My humans have been married for some time now, and I must say they appear to be doing rather well.

They still choose each other.

They still drink coffee together.

And, most importantly, they have both accepted that I am part of the management structure.

That last point should not be underestimated.

This morning, while I was carrying out my usual inspection of the garden, the red tom appeared again.

There he was, strolling through my grounds as if no special anniversary regulations were in force.

Really.

One would think he might have shown a little respect.

I kept a very close eye on him from indoors, naturally.

At some point during this important security operation, my male human picked me up.

Again.

I am still not entirely sure why he does this.

Perhaps anniversaries make humans sentimental.

Perhaps he simply wished to hold something beautiful.

I shall allow him that interpretation.

After all, today is his special day too.

The celebrations also included coffee, which I strongly approve of because coffee in this household comes with a most sensible tradition.

My humans have coffee.

I receive small treats.

This arrangement works extremely well and, in my opinion, is exactly the sort of cooperation upon which successful marriages are built.

Give and take.

Compromise.

Mutual respect.

And snacks.

So today I shall be slightly more generous than usual with my household evaluations.

The red tom will remain under surveillance.

The male human may continue his occasional lifting privileges.

And both my humans may take the evening off from training.

They have, after all, achieved something rather lovely together.

Happy wedding anniversary, my humans.

You chose each other wisely.

And later, of course, you chose me.

Which means the household is now exactly as it should be.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🐟Household Policy Update: The Open-Door Night Shift
items.content_html:
I am pleased to report that the recent decision to leave the doors open at night has been met with my approval.

Naturally, I do not sleep in just one place. That would suggest a lack of options, and I have worked far too hard on this household to tolerate such restrictions.

Some nights I select the sofa. On others, a chair, a quiet corner, or another carefully chosen location that happens to meet my requirements at that precise moment. Comfort must be assessed continuously. A proper ruler does not simply go to bed. She conducts overnight inspections.

The open-door arrangement therefore suits me rather well. I can move freely through my household, check that everything remains where I left it and select whichever sleeping quarters deserve the honour of my presence.

My humans may even believe this means they can enjoy an uninterrupted night.

Bless them.

Because regardless of where I have chosen to sleep, one household rule remains completely unchanged.

At 06:30 sharp, I am on the bed.

Not 06:27, because I am not unreasonable.

Not 06:35, because standards must be maintained.

06:30.

That is breakfast time.

I consider punctuality one of the most important qualities in human staff, so I make a point of being there personally to supervise the start of the morning shift.

Doors may remain open.

Sleeping arrangements may remain flexible.

But breakfast?

Breakfast is governed by the clock.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

Naturally, I do not sleep in just one place. That would suggest a lack of options, and I have worked far too hard on this household to tolerate such restrictions.

Some nights I select the sofa. On others, a chair, a quiet corner, or another carefully chosen location that happens to meet my requirements at that precise moment. Comfort must be assessed continuously. A proper ruler does not simply go to bed. She conducts overnight inspections.

The open-door arrangement therefore suits me rather well. I can move freely through my household, check that everything remains where I left it and select whichever sleeping quarters deserve the honour of my presence.

My humans may even believe this means they can enjoy an uninterrupted night.

Bless them.

Because regardless of where I have chosen to sleep, one household rule remains completely unchanged.

At 06:30 sharp, I am on the bed.

Not 06:27, because I am not unreasonable.

Not 06:35, because standards must be maintained.

06:30.

That is breakfast time.

I consider punctuality one of the most important qualities in human staff, so I make a point of being there personally to supervise the start of the morning shift.

Doors may remain open.

Sleeping arrangements may remain flexible.

But breakfast?

Breakfast is governed by the clock.

Yours,
Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🎂A Birthday Audience for the Male-Human
items.content_html:
Today is a particularly important date in the household calendar: the male-human is celebrating his birthday.

Naturally, I have dressed for the occasion in my finest white outfit. It is freshly arranged, beautifully fluffed and, as always, entirely bespoke. Some creatures require wardrobes. I simply wake up looking magnificent.

In honour of his special day, I have also decided to be on my very best behaviour. I shall refrain from unnecessary complaints, surprise inspections and dramatic disapproval. I may even make myself slightly more accessible than usual.

This is, of course, an exceptional birthday privilege and should not be mistaken for a permanent change in household policy.

This evening, there will be a proper birthday defilé. Guests will arrive to present themselves before the household, admire the decorations and, one assumes, pay their respects to the birthday human and his elegant white supervisor.

I am particularly pleased to hear that there will be delicious drinks and finger food. The humans may believe these refreshments are intended for the guests, but every successful reception requires strict quality control.

Should a small canapé, slice of chicken or other suitable item happen to be left unattended, I may be required to investigate. This is not stealing. It is an emergency catering inspection.

Throughout the evening, I may also suddenly materialise behind guests at entirely unpredictable moments.

This has nothing whatsoever to do with the food they are holding.

I shall simply be checking posture, plate security and general compliance with household regulations. It is pure coincidence that these inspections are most frequent near cheese, chicken and anything served on a small decorative stick.

Naturally, if an item then disappears, I cannot possibly be held to blame. The evidence would be entirely circumstantial. There may have been crumbs near my whiskers, but crumbs travel. A plate may have moved slightly, but plates are notoriously unreliable witnesses.

Furthermore, any guest careless enough to abandon finger food within royal reach must accept a certain degree of personal responsibility. One cannot leave valuable refreshments unguarded in a professionally managed household and then act surprised when management intervenes.

I shall therefore accept no blame whatsoever.

At most, I might accept a small consultancy fee.

I shall circulate among the visitors, receive compliments graciously and allow selected guests the honour of approaching me. Those who understand proper etiquette may even receive a brief audience.

Happy birthday to my dear male-human. Today, I shall permit him to feel like the most important person in the house.

At least until bedtime.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

Birthdays are lovely, but standards must be maintained.

items.title: 📝🐱🏡 From Jutta to Mrs. Cotton
items.content_html:
There was a time, before I took up my present royal appointment, when I lived in Enschede and answered to the name Jutta.

It was a perfectly respectable name, of course. Nothing wrong with it at all. But when my future humans came to meet me, they immediately understood something rather important: I was not Jutta.

I was Mrs. Cotton.

Some humans require months of training before they recognise authority. Mine showed unusual promise from the beginning.

On march 11th, I was officially adopted and transferred to my new household. I was 3 years old at the time, although I already possessed the judgement, dignity and household-management skills of a much more experienced lady.

Naturally, my humans believed they were bringing me home.

In reality, I was taking possession of the property.

Since then, I have settled in extremely well. My humans provide comfortable furniture, warm sleeping places and a generally acceptable level of personal service. Meals are served, doors are opened and cushions are adjusted according to my requirements. Their performance is not always flawless, but I believe strongly in continuing education.

They are kind, loving and very devoted to me, which is exactly as it should be.

I am the only child in the household, and I take that responsibility seriously. I supervise the living room, inspect all new objects and ensure that no human sits comfortably without first considering whether I might need the space.

Life here is good. I am safe, loved and properly appreciated. My humans may have adopted me from Enschede, but we all know the truth.

They did not simply choose a cat.

They recognised their queen.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🐮Household Policy Update: Patience, Plastic Surgery and Proper Access
items.content_html:
Miss Moo Moo Longtail has once again been under the knife.

Plastic surgery, no less.

Fortunately, my humans performed the operation rather well. I supervised from a suitable distance, naturally. A ruler must allow her staff to develop confidence, even when they are repairing important members of the royal household.

Miss Moo Moo Longtail is recovering nicely, although I shall continue to inspect the stitching. Quality control is one of my many duties.

There has also been promising progress regarding the temperature of my residence. It now appears that air conditioning may actually be installed. My humans have listened to me, which was inevitable. It simply took them a little while to realise that my thoughtful observations were not casual suggestions but official royal instructions.

I have now been here for five months. Five months already. Time passes remarkably quickly when one is reorganising an entire household.

So far, so good.

The place is beginning to run according to my standards. Every morning at approximately 6.30, I wake my humans for breakfast. They do not always respond immediately, but after a period of firm encouragement, one of them eventually comes downstairs.

Progress cannot be rushed.

Today, I overheard them discussing the possibility of leaving the doors open permanently. This would, of course, be a considerable improvement. A queen should not have to wait for doors to be opened inside her own palace. Free access between rooms is not a luxury. It is basic feline infrastructure.

My humans may believe these changes are their own ideas. I see no reason to correct them. Good leadership often means allowing one’s staff to feel involved.

And so, after five months of patient training, carefully timed morning instructions and the occasional firm stare, my household is slowly becoming fit for royal occupation.

Patience is indeed a virtue.

Although ruling with a steel paw certainly helps.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

P.S. Photographic evidence of Miss Moo Moo Longtail’s successful reconstructive surgery is attached. Please admire the workmanship and refrain from asking too many questions about how the injury occurred. The investigation remains ongoing, and all evidence against me is entirely circumstantial.

items.title: 📝🐱🇳🇴A Royal Reply to the Nieces of the North
items.content_html:
My Dearest Nieces of the North,

I was utterly delighted to receive your handwritten communication in the form of a proper letter. In an age when humans insist on tapping hurried little messages into glowing screens, it was most refreshing to receive something created with genuine care, patience and excellent penmanship.

Please know that you are always most welcome in my household. Your presence was not merely appreciated, but deeply honoured. It is a rare privilege for visitors to be admitted into my kingdom, observe my household management at close quarters and, most importantly, receive my personal approval. You both conducted yourselves splendidly.

I am also pleased to report that the Snack Acquisition Programme has been a tremendous success. The recently achieved 40 per cent increase in snacks is certainly encouraging, although naturally I consider it only the beginning. There remains considerable room for growth, and I trust that my humans will continue to take their responsibilities seriously.

Your wonderful works of art are now proudly displayed in the household. They are truly magnificent creations, beautifully handmade and clearly produced by artists of great talent and refined judgement. I inspect them regularly during my royal rounds and am pleased to confirm that they have greatly improved the cultural standing of my residence.

Thank you once again for your lovely letter, your delightful company and your most valuable contribution to both the household art collection and the snack economy.

You shall always be welcome here.

With royal affection and firm but fair approval,

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱⚡A Most Unusual Royal Arrival
items.content_html:
King Charles and Queen Camilla appeared at the opening of the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow by stepping out of Doctor Who’s TARDIS.

As a fellow head of state, I must admit this was an impressive entrance. Arriving officially by blue time machine is difficult to surpass, although I personally prefer to materialise silently behind my humans while they are eating.

It creates much the same sense of wonder, with considerably less paperwork.

Still, I applaud Their Majesties for embracing unconventional royal transport. A monarch should always keep the household guessing. Today, a golden carriage. Tomorrow, a time machine. In my own kingdom, I alternate between the sofa, the windowsill and a cardboard box which, for reasons of national security, is far larger on the inside.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🫯Household Policy Update: The Ginger Intruder
items.content_html:
A ginger tom from the neighbourhood came to assist me with an unexpected security inspection today.

Naturally, this involved enormous tails, several firm hisses and a considerable amount of highly professional staring. My humans appeared concerned, but they do not always understand advanced feline diplomacy.

Allow me to reassure everyone that this was completely normal.

The tom had entered my territory and therefore required a clear explanation of the household hierarchy. I delivered this explanation personally, with excellent posture and a tail approximately three times its usual size.

There was no panic.

There was no loss of control.

There was merely a formal boundary meeting between two senior cats, one of whom had temporarily forgotten that I am in charge.

He now knows his place.

Afterwards, I spent roughly an hour and a half walking through the room, checking every corner and sniffing absolutely everything. This was not nervousness. It was a full post-incident security audit.

A responsible ruler must ensure that no ginger influence remains hidden behind a chair, beneath a table or near the curtains.

The room has now been declared safe.

My authority remains intact.

The tom has been appropriately briefed.

And my humans have earned several continuing education points in the subject of perfectly normal cat behaviour.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🌙 Late Night Household Report
items.content_html:
By the time my humans believe the house has settled for the night, my real work begins.

At precisely the moment they switch off the lights and whisper, “Goodnight,” I commence the final inspection of my kingdom.

The female human turns over exactly seven times before accepting that I have already selected the best part of the bed.

The male human continues to insist that the duvet belongs equally to everyone. This is an ambitious theory, unsupported by either history or current practice.

Both humans appear convinced that I spend the night sleeping.

This is adorable.

In reality, I conduct routine patrols of every room, inspect the water bowl for quality assurance, verify that no suspicious insects have entered the premises, and ensure every window remains exactly as it was when I checked it fifteen minutes earlier.

Around three o’clock I also perform a silent observation exercise by sitting beside the bed and gazing thoughtfully at whichever human appears least prepared for unexpected eye contact.

There is no need to wake them.

It is simply important that they know they are being monitored.

At approximately four-thirty I conclude that breakfast is now a matter of strategic importance rather than chronology.

The humans may refer to this as “far too early.”

I prefer to call it proactive meal planning.

Overall assessment of the night shift:

Security: Excellent.

Blanket ownership: Successfully maintained.

Human awareness: Requires further training.

Breakfast punctuality: Deeply disappointing.

Another productive evening in the service of my household.

Yours,

Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱My Official Complaint About Vacuum Cleaners
items.content_html:
Yesterday, my humans committed the same household offence they have committed many times before.

They brought out the vacuum cleaner.

I was resting peacefully, supervising the living room from a strategically selected position, when the machine appeared without warning. No consultation. No written notice. Not even a polite request for approval.

Then it began.

The noise was entirely unreasonable. It roared across my kingdom as if the carpet had personally offended it. Chairs were moved. Cushions were lifted. Dust was pursued with a level of determination my humans rarely show when I request an early dinner.

Naturally, I withdrew to a secure observation point.

This was not fear. I would like that entered into the official record.

It was a tactical relocation.

From a safe distance, I monitored the operation carefully. The vacuum cleaner moved from room to room, swallowing crumbs, fluff and several perfectly respectable pieces of floor decoration that I had been keeping for administrative purposes.

My humans seemed pleased with themselves afterwards. They admired the clean carpet and spoke proudly about how fresh everything looked.

Fresh?

The entire house smelled suspiciously of effort.

I do understand that household maintenance is sometimes necessary. A well-run palace requires standards. However, I must insist on a few improvements.

First, all future vacuuming sessions must be announced at least one nap in advance.

Second, my current sleeping place must be declared a protected royal zone.

Third, any treats offered afterwards must be considered compensation, not bribery.

I have placed both humans on a short remedial training programme. Their continuing education points will remain under review until they demonstrate better judgement.

For now, I have returned to the living room and inspected their work.

The carpet is acceptable.

The disturbance was not.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🛌🏻The Saturday Morning Wake-Up Department
items.content_html:
Saturday mornings are an important part of my household administration.

My humans seem to believe that Saturday is a day for “sleeping in”. This is a charming idea, rather like believing the sofa belongs to them.

At precisely the correct hour, which is whenever I decide the household has been inactive for long enough, I begin my inspection.

First, I sit beside the bed and observe.

Nothing.

Then I walk across the duvet with the careful authority of a royal official checking a suspicious bridge. One human moves slightly, but this is clearly not sufficient.

I therefore proceed to Phase Two: Strategic Proximity.

This involves sitting very close to a human face and staring with quiet determination. Humans find this surprisingly effective. Perhaps they sense the weight of responsibility. Perhaps they simply notice my whiskers.

Eventually, one eye opens.

“Cotton, it’s Saturday.”

Yes. I am aware of the calendar. I personally approved it.

The human closes the eye again.

A serious management error.

I then take up position on the chest, where I can monitor breathing, facial expressions and any signs of breakfast-related activity. I am not heavy, of course. I am merely impossible to ignore.

At last, the humans surrender and leave the bed.

They shuffle towards the kitchen looking tired and confused, while I lead the procession with dignity. Another successful morning operation.

Breakfast is served. Curtains are opened. The household begins moving.

And my humans receive valuable continuing education points for responding to senior leadership before noon.

Firm but fair. That is my policy.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.content_html:
The weekend is nearly upon us, which means my humans will once again be at home for a full twenty-four hours a day.

A queen must make sacrifices for her household.

items.content_html:
Last night, the Nieces of the North came by for one final farewell before setting off on the very long day ahead of them.

Quite right too.

It is therefore essential that their supervisor returns promptly to restore order, review current procedures and remind everyone exactly who is in charge.

I wish the Nieces a safe journey and their feline manager a successful return to office.

No doubt the household will be back under firm and fair paw before bedtime.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🫟The Exterior Painter’s Unexpected Promotion
items.content_html:
At first, I regarded the exterior painter with the caution appropriate for any tradesman arriving at my residence with ladders, brushes and suspiciously energetic footwear.

He made noises outside my windows, moved objects without submitting the correct paperwork and appeared at several unexpected heights. Naturally, I placed him under observation.

However, I am a fair ruler, and I believe in allowing staff the opportunity to improve.

To his credit, the exterior painter has made remarkable progress. He now enters calmly, speaks to me in a respectful tone and, most importantly, understands that a proper working day must include time devoted to stroking the household’s senior management.

This explains why I am suddenly sitting beside him on the chair.

It is not friendship in the ordinary sense. It is a probationary executive arrangement.

He has a warm arm, a steady hand and a cup of tea, all of which suggest good judgement. Furthermore, sitting beside him allows me to supervise both the painter and my human simultaneously. Efficiency is one of my greatest strengths.

My human may look surprised, but that is because humans often mistake careful diplomacy for inconsistency. I have not changed my mind without reason. The painter has simply completed the required training modules and collected enough continuing education points to qualify for limited royal access.

He may now stroke my head, admire me at close range and share my chair, provided he remembers that it is, in fact, my chair.

The exterior painter has therefore been officially promoted from Suspicious Outdoor Person to Approved Temporary Household Associate.

A considerable honour.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🚪The Closed Door Policy
items.content_html:
Humans do not understand closed doors.

They believe a door is simply either open or shut. A practical household object. Very sweet.

To a cat, however, a closed door is a formal challenge to authority.

In my household, I deal with this personally. I sit outside the offending door and issue one clear instruction. If my humans fail to respond, I repeat it at increasing volume while placing one paw beneath the door for emphasis.

Naturally, the moment they open it, I do not necessarily wish to enter. That is not the point.

The point is that all areas of my kingdom must remain available for inspection at all times.

My humans are improving. Slowly.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱🍬Lessons from the Nieces of the North
items.content_html:
I recently had the great pleasure of meeting family from the North of Norway, including two particularly impressive young ladies whom I shall refer to as the Nieces of the North.

They were kind, gentle and clearly well educated in the most important area of household life: obtaining treats from humans.

I watched them carefully.

Without causing alarm, making formal demands or submitting a written request to management, they somehow persuaded the humans to produce one delicacy after another. It was a masterclass in negotiation. A glance here, a charming smile there, and suddenly snacks appeared.

Naturally, I took notes.

A competent ruler must always remain open to new leadership techniques, especially when they involve food. Since their visit, I have tested several of their methods on my own humans, and I am pleased to report excellent results.

Clever girls.

They were also wonderfully sweet to me, and I very much enjoyed sitting near them. I do not offer my company lightly, of course. My presence is a privilege, carefully allocated according to character, manners and respect for personal space. The Nieces passed their assessment with distinction.

Later that evening, the parents of the Nieces arrived.

At first, I kept a dignified distance and watched proceedings carefully. One should never rush an inspection of new humans. I observed their movements, listened to their voices and considered whether they understood the correct protocols for entering my household.

Once I was satisfied that everything appeared to be in order, I carried out a brief personal check.

They passed too.

All in all, the visit was a tremendous success. I gained new friends, improved my treat-acquisition strategy and maintained excellent diplomatic relations with the North of Norway.

I sincerely hope the Nieces of the North will return before too long. Their company was delightful, their manners were excellent, and their knowledge of human snack management was truly inspiring.

Yours,

Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🇳🇴🐱The Northern Delegation Arrives
items.content_html:
Today, my Palace is preparing for a most distinguished visit.

The Norwegian Family has arrived in the Netherlands. Not the Norwegian Royal Family, I hasten to add. They may perhaps visit me at a later date, once they have reviewed their household arrangements and ensured that every member of their party is suitably trained for an audience with a cat of my standing.

No, today’s visitors are our own Norwegian family members from the high north, which is far more exciting.

I am especially curious about the two nieces. I have heard excellent reports about these young ladies, but naturally I shall conduct my own assessment. I shall observe their manners, their ability to admire me without excessive squealing, and whether they understand that the finest seat in the room may already be occupied.

They are arriving this afternoon, which means my humans have been placed on full Palace-preparation duties.

The floors must be vacuumed. The furniture must be dusted. Cushions must be arranged with military precision, although not so precisely that I cannot immediately rearrange them. Every room must appear welcoming, elegant and entirely free of the small white hairs that mysteriously gather throughout my kingdom.

I have appointed myself Chief Inspector of Domestic Readiness.

This is a demanding role. I must supervise the vacuum cleaner from a safe distance, inspect freshly cleaned surfaces by walking across them, and ensure that no blanket is folded without first being tested for comfort.

Later in the evening, the parents of these remarkable young ladies will also arrive to take part in the Royal banquet.

I am told this involves bread, fillings and pleasant conversation. I shall therefore position myself nearby as the official quality controller. It would be irresponsible to allow a banquet to proceed without careful feline oversight, particularly when chicken, cheese or butter may be involved.

Everything must be ready at the highest level of alertness.

The Palace will shine. The table will be prepared. The humans will be presentable. And I shall be waiting in my finest white coat to welcome our northern guests with warmth, dignity and just the right amount of royal curiosity.

After all, family visits are very special.

Especially when everyone remembers whom they have truly come to see.

Med kongelig hilsen, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🇳🇴👑

items.title: 📝🐱The Great Fuss About Fifty
items.content_html:
A member of my family has turned fifty.

Apparently, this is an Event.

There have been discussions, decorations, secret arrangements and a remarkable amount of excitement over a number. My humans keep saying, “You only turn fifty once,” as though they have uncovered a rare scientific phenomenon.

Naturally, I have examined this claim.

You only turn fifty-one once as well.

And fifty-two.

In fact, unless the humans have discovered a highly unusual way of repeating birthdays, every age occurs only once. Yet nobody appears to be planning a grand banquet for turning forty-seven and three quarters.

Humans are very selective about mathematics.

Still, I understand that fifty is considered a milestone. Humans enjoy milestones because they give them an excuse to gather together, eat cake and tell stories about how young they still feel. They also enjoy saying things such as, “Fifty is the new forty,” which raises several administrative questions about what has happened to forty.

From my position as head of household, I have decided to permit the celebrations.

After all, reaching fifty requires years of effort, patience and, presumably, surviving a great many poorly organised birthdays. That deserves recognition.

There should be cake. There should be presents. There should be comfortable seating and a sensible schedule that does not interfere with my afternoon rest.

Most importantly, the birthday person should enjoy every moment. Not because fifty is more special than fifty-one, but because being loved is worth making a fuss about at any age.

Although next year, when everyone says, “It’s only fifty-one,” I shall remind them that one only turns fifty-one once.

Consistency is essential in a well-managed family.

Yours,

Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

ps. I’ll be watching you about weird claims and ages.

items.title: 📝🐱🪰Why Fly Hunting Is an Essential Royal Duty
items.content_html:
Some humans believe that fly hunting is merely a hobby.

This is incorrect.

Fly hunting is a vital household service, performed by highly trained feline personnel. In my household, that personnel happens to be me.

A fly is not simply an insect. It is an uninvited aerial intruder with no respect for boundaries, quiet afternoons or royal airspace. It enters without an appointment, circles the lamps and behaves as though the entire living room belongs to it.

Naturally, I must intervene.

First, fly hunting provides excellent physical exercise. A successful operation may involve sprinting, leaping, climbing and staring intensely at the ceiling for several minutes. Humans often pay for gym memberships to achieve less.

Second, it sharpens the mind. A fly changes direction without warning, disappears behind curtains and repeatedly ignores formal requests to leave. Tracking such an opponent requires patience, strategy and exceptional leadership.

Third, fly hunting protects my humans. They may claim they are perfectly capable of dealing with a fly themselves, but their preferred method usually involves waving a tea towel and knocking over something decorative. It is therefore safer for everyone if I take command.

There is also the matter of morale. Nothing brings a household together quite like watching me launch myself heroically towards a window while both humans shout, “Careful!”

Their concern is touching, although unnecessary.

Of course, not every hunt ends in capture. Sometimes the fly escapes. This does not mean the operation has failed. It simply means I have issued a warning and demonstrated control of the territory.

Fly hunting is not play.

It is security, exercise, enrichment and public service.

And, frankly, my humans should be grateful that I provide all four without sending them an invoice.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾🪰

items.title: 📝🐱The Melon, the Sunbeams and the Suspicious Painter
items.content_html:
Every morning, I begin my duties with a thorough inspection of the kitchen.

Some cats rush about demanding breakfast. I prefer to position myself elegantly on the kitchen worktop and allow breakfast negotiations to develop at their own pace. A true ruler never appears desperate. She simply sits near the food cupboards and looks increasingly disappointed.

This particular morning, the sun was shining through the stained glass, scattering warm, coloured beams across my white fur. Naturally, I placed myself directly in the finest patch of light.

Good lighting is essential when one is conducting important household business.

Beside me sat a melon.

I settled slightly behind it, with only my ears visible above the top. From the humans’ point of view, the melon had suddenly grown two small white ears.

They found this extremely amusing.

I allowed them their little moment.

In reality, I was testing a new surveillance technique: agricultural camouflage. No visiting sparrow, passing neighbour or unauthorised kitchen snack would ever suspect that the melon was being supervised by senior management.

Later that day, one of my humans presented me with a Vitakraft stick.

Now, I am normally a calm and dignified lady. I believe in patience, good manners and measured responses.

But there are certain delicacies for which one might, purely hypothetically, commit a minor act of treason.

The Vitakraft stick is one of them.

I took possession immediately and conducted a full quality inspection. The flavour was excellent, the texture satisfactory and the human’s delivery speed just within acceptable limits.

I awarded several continuing education points.

However, there was no time for a prolonged celebration. The outside painter had arrived.

A stranger.

Near my house.

With ladders.

Clearly, this required my personal attention.

I moved to the nearest window and watched him carefully. Every brushstroke was monitored. Every movement was recorded. Every suspicious bucket was examined from a safe and comfortable distance.

The humans claimed he was simply painting the outside of the house.

That is exactly what an outside painter would want them to think.

Fortunately, I remained on duty until the situation was under control.

By evening, the melon had been cleared of suspicion, the Vitakraft stick had vanished without witnesses, and the painter had completed his work under strict royal supervision.

Another successful day of household management.

Honestly, I do not know how my humans managed before me.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

Yesterday, my household received a specialist visitor.

A furniture restorer arrived to inspect the sofa armrest, which bears an important piece of historical artwork created by Snickers. My humans refer to it as “damage”. I prefer the more accurate term: an original mixed-media installation exploring texture, ownership and feline determination.

Snickers, a distinguished grey tabby who ruled this household for eighteen and a half years, clearly believed that an ordinary sofa required artistic direction. She therefore devoted herself to improving one particular armrest, thread by thread, with the patience of a master craftswoman.

The restorer examined her work very carefully.

He looked at it from several angles. He touched the fabric. He considered the structure beneath it. My humans stood nearby with the solemn expressions usually reserved for museum curators discussing the restoration of a national treasure.

I supervised from a suitable distance.

Naturally, I was interested in the professional assessment. Not because I have ever scratched a sofa myself, of course. I merely believe that a responsible head of household should understand all aspects of furniture conservation.

The restorer explained what could be repaired, replaced and strengthened. My humans listened attentively, although I noticed that nobody asked the most important question: how much of Snickers’ original artistic vision should remain visible for future generations?

Restoration is a delicate matter. Remove too much and you erase history. Remove too little and visitors may continue to ask whether the sofa was attacked by a very small, highly focused tiger.

I believe a tasteful compromise is required.

The armrest should be made comfortable and respectable again, while retaining perhaps one tiny thread as a memorial to Snickers and her uncompromising approach to interior design.

As for me, I remain entirely innocent in all furniture-related matters. Any marks discovered during future inspections will require a separate investigation, proper documentation and considerably more evidence.

Until then, I shall continue my duties as guardian of the sofa.

From the softest cushion, naturally.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱Household Policy Update: The Approved Sleeping Places
items.content_html:
There appears to be some confusion in my household regarding sleeping arrangements.

My humans seem to believe that I have “a bed”.

This is technically correct in the same way that Buckingham Palace technically has “a chair”. One does not restrict oneself unnecessarily.

As head of the household, I am responsible for inspecting every possible resting location. The sofa must be tested. The armchair must be assessed. Freshly folded laundry requires immediate quality control. Human pillows must be checked for softness, warmth and whether they have been positioned inconveniently close to a human head.

This is not indecision. It is governance.

My humans have also developed the curious habit of saying things such as, “I was sitting there.”

I fail to see the relevance.

A chair is not occupied merely because a human was sitting on it moments ago. Once vacated, it returns to royal ownership. This is basic household law and really should have been covered during their initial training.

Naturally, certain sleeping places are more desirable when they are urgently required by someone else. A laptop bag becomes especially comfortable five minutes before departure. A clean jumper is at its finest just before it is worn. The centre of the bed reaches peak quality when both humans are attempting to sleep.

Timing is an important part of leadership.

For clarity, I have now approved the following locations for my personal use: all chairs, all cushions, both sides of the bed, the middle of the bed, any blanket currently in use, all freshly laundered clothing and any cardboard box entering the premises.

My actual cat bed remains available for decorative purposes.

I trust this policy update will prevent further misunderstandings.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱The Royal Soup Signal
items.content_html:
My humans have recently noticed that, when I am presented with a deliciously cold soup during warm weather, my tail begins to tick and pulse.

They appear to find this mysterious.

It is not mysterious. It is communication.

A rapidly trembling tail would suggest excessive excitement, which would be undignified. A completely still tail, however, might imply that I had failed to notice the arrival of refreshments. Therefore, I employ a subtle rhythmic movement of the tip.

It means:

“The temperature is acceptable.”

“The aroma has been noted.”

“You may place the bowl before me.”

“And yes, your annual performance review is improving.”

Humans often wag entire limbs when pleased. They clap, wave, dance and occasionally announce that something is “absolutely lovely”. I prefer efficiency. A few precise taps of the tail communicate everything required without compromising my royal composure.

The pulsing also helps me concentrate. Receiving soup is not merely eating. It involves inspection, temperature assessment, portion evaluation and careful consideration of whether a second serving should be authorised.

During hot weather, cold soup is particularly important. I am a white indoor cat wearing a permanent fur coat. I cannot simply remove a cardigan or complain dramatically beside an electric fan. My cooling arrangements must therefore be handled by trained household staff.

So when my tail begins ticking, my humans should not stare.

They should take notes.

The signal means that their chilled soup initiative has received provisional royal approval.

Provisionally, of course. Continued approval may require another bowl.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱The Importance of Midnight Zoomies for Fitness and Morale
items.content_html:
There comes a moment in every well-managed household when the lights are low, the humans are settled, and peace appears to have been declared.

This is, naturally, the ideal time for high-speed operations.

My midnight zoomies are not random. They are a carefully structured programme designed to maintain my physical condition, sharpen my reflexes and remind the household that authority remains fully operational after dark.

The route is selected with precision. I begin in the bedroom, accelerate through the hallway, perform a controlled turn beside the living room furniture and conclude with an impressive leap onto a strategically chosen surface. Sometimes this surface contains a sleeping human. That is not poor planning. It is an advanced morale exercise.

My humans occasionally wake with a startled expression, as though an indoor cat travelling at considerable speed is somehow unexpected. This shows that their continuing education remains incomplete.

Night-time exercise offers several important benefits. It keeps the legs strong, the whiskers alert and the mind focused. It also prevents complacency among staff. A household that knows its ruler may thunder through the corridor at any hour is a household that remains disciplined.

There is also the matter of morale. During the day, my humans are burdened with work, errands and various unnecessary concerns. At night, I provide excitement, movement and the unforgettable sound of paws racing across the floor.

This is not disruption. It is enrichment.

After completing my fitness programme, I usually stop suddenly, wash one shoulder and look entirely innocent. Any suggestion that I have caused chaos is based on circumstantial evidence.

I then retire to bed, refreshed and satisfied, while my humans attempt to understand what has just happened.

They need not worry. Their queen is fit, morale is high, and the kingdom remains secure.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱Household Policy Update: Touching Is a Privilege, Not a Subscription
items.content_html:
I feel it is time to address a matter which continues to confuse my humans.

Apparently, they have noticed that when my food is being served, I am perfectly happy to be picked up, stroked, cuddled and generally admired at close range.

Quite right too.

At mealtimes, I am operating under special diplomatic conditions.

Food is being prepared. Bowls are moving. Cupboards are opening. Important smells are circulating through my household. This is not the moment for unnecessary distance between senior management and catering staff.

So yes, during food service, my humans may pick me up.

They may stroke me.

They may hold me close.

I may even appear unusually tolerant while inspecting the situation from their arms.

This is entirely normal.

I am simply maintaining direct oversight of the catering department.

However, once the meal has been served and consumed, normal household regulations immediately resume.

And under normal regulations, I prefer my humans to remain at a respectful distance.

Not because I do not love them.

Good heavens, no.

I love them enormously.

From over there.

The difficulty is that humans have developed a rather strange idea about affection. They seem to believe that because a cat enjoyed being stroked at 8:03 in the morning, this automatically grants them touching rights at 10:17, 13:42 and again during an important afternoon sleep.

It does not.

Affection is not a season ticket.

There is a very simple system in my household.

When I walk towards my humans and stop beside them, I am available.

When I stand close enough to be touched, permission may reasonably be assumed.

When I lean against a leg, present my head or remain in place after first contact, the interaction may continue.

This is what we call a clear application procedure.

By contrast, when I am sitting peacefully three feet away, this does not mean:

“Please come and fetch me.”

When I am walking through the room, it does not mean:

“Excellent opportunity for an unexpected cuddle.”

And when I am asleep, it most certainly does not mean:

“Let us see how much affection we can insert into this situation before she wakes up.”

No.

The rule is beautifully simple.

I come to you.

That is how I show trust.

That is how I choose contact.

That is how civilised affection works.

My humans are, of course, still learning.

Sometimes I see one of them looking at me from across the room with that particular expression. The one that says, “She looks so soft.”

Naturally I look soft.

I am white, elegant and exceptionally well maintained.

That is not an invitation.

It is a visual experience.

Please enjoy it responsibly.

So let us put an end to this human confusion once and for all.

Yes, you may cuddle me while food is being served.

Yes, I may stand beside you later and request affection.

And yes, for the rest of the day I may prefer a tasteful amount of personal space.

These things are not contradictory.

They are called boundaries, timing and excellent household management.

Honestly, I do not know why this is so difficult.

Still, every misunderstanding is a training opportunity.

My humans have earned another continuing education point.

Not enough for independent touching privileges, obviously.

But progress is progress.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱Settling In Nicely, Thank You Very Much
items.content_html:
On 11 March, I was collected from the shelter and brought to what my humans rather casually call “home”.

I prefer to think of it as my new location.

Naturally, one does not simply move into a property without carrying out a full inspection. There are standards to maintain, comfort levels to assess, staff to observe and, most importantly, several highly suspicious corners that require immediate investigation.

I am pleased to report that I have settled in extremely well.

The location is acceptable.

More than acceptable, actually.

The humans are also beginning to settle in nicely.

They do try.

I can see that.

There are plenty of toys, which suggests that someone has at least attempted to prepare for my arrival. Mice, balls, dangling things, rolling things and various brightly coloured objects apparently designed by committees who have never actually met a cat.

And yet, after careful testing by senior management, my favourite toy is…

a simple ping-pong ball.

Of course it is.

It rolls beautifully, changes direction without warning, disappears under furniture and creates exactly the right amount of household disruption. A highly sophisticated piece of equipment, despite what the humans may think.

I have also explored the entire house.

Thoroughly.

Professionally.

Room by room.

This includes the bedroom, where I am apparently “not allowed”.

An interesting policy.

I reviewed it personally.

Several times.

I remain unconvinced.

Still, my humans are new to this arrangement and require continuing education points. One cannot expect perfection immediately.

There is, however, one unresolved matter.

I have been informed that the house also has an attic.

And indeed, there is one door that has remained firmly closed since my arrival.

One door.

Always closed.

Naturally, I have noticed.

I notice everything.

What is behind it? Boxes? Dust? Ancient treasures? Secret emergency supplies of cat food? A second, even better household?

At present, I cannot say.

But I have only lived here since 11 March.

There is time.

The location is good.

The humans are trying.

The ping-pong ball is excellent.

And the closed door?

Well.

Every kingdom has one mystery.

For now.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱The Exterior Decorator Requires Close Supervision
items.content_html:
Today, my humans witnessed what they have rather foolishly described as “me getting on very well with the exterior painter”.

I must correct the record.

There was no affection involved.

Yes, I gave him several head bumps. This was not cuddling. It was a professional identification procedure. A contractor entering my estate must, naturally, be marked with the official household scent before being permitted to continue his duties.

Yes, I also ran past him at considerable speed.

Again, this has been misunderstood.

I was conducting a series of rapid-response perimeter checks, designed to assess his reflexes, general awareness and ability to remain calm when senior management suddenly appears at ankle height.

He performed reasonably well.

I may also have passed him several times for no obvious reason. There was, of course, an obvious reason. I was monitoring workflow, inspecting access routes and making certain he understood that although my humans may have hired him, he was working on my building.

At one point, I believe he may even have thought I liked him.

Charming.

I do not “like” contractors. I evaluate them.

Still, he has shown promise. He appears polite, accepts surprise inspections without complaint and has so far resisted the human tendency to interfere with my movements.

Therefore, I have granted him temporary status as an Approved Exterior Maintenance Person, Second Class.

Further head bumps may occur.

Strictly for administrative purposes.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱A Rare Case of Humans Thinking Properly
items.content_html:
As Head of Household Strategy, Senior Director of Sofa Allocation and sole authority on whether a meeting could have been a nap, I am naturally cautious when recommending human work.

Standards must be maintained.

However, during one of my routine inspections of the internet, I came across DESIGN THINKING! Comic, and I must admit something rather unusual happened.

I approved.

This is a comic about design, technology, work, AI, meetings, engagement, hiring and all the other fascinating systems humans have invented to make simple things require twelve stakeholders and a colourful diagram.

Naturally, I felt seen.

The humour is clever, painfully observant and often has that excellent quality of making you laugh first and then stare quietly into the middle distance because, regrettably, it is true.

But my relationship with The Artist is, I should point out, not merely professional admiration from afar.

The Artist has made my portrait.

Yes.

My portrait.

This came about because my humans, after years of continuing education, finally demonstrated a promising moment of initiative. They had been following the work of DESIGN THINKING! Comic and, in a rare example of independent thought, wondered whether The Artist might consider capturing my likeness.

I allowed them to enquire.

One must encourage progress.

Naturally, the project required careful preparation. Suitable photographs had to be selected. My colouring, expression and general air of senior authority had to be properly represented. I supervised this process closely, mainly by being unavailable whenever anyone wished to take a useful photograph.

This is called maintaining creative tension.

Then came the extraordinary part.

The Artist looked at me, understood the brief and created a portrait that somehow captured not merely a white cat, but the unmistakable presence of a household executive who has had quite enough of everyone’s excuses.

I was impressed.

My humans were delighted.

I remained professionally composed.

There may have been a moment of prolonged staring at the finished artwork, but this should not be interpreted emotionally. I was conducting quality assurance.

The portrait now has a very special place in my household, because there is something rather wonderful about being seen through the eyes of an artist whose work you already admire.

Especially when those eyes correctly identify you as management.

items.title: 📝🐱That Tiny Meow at the Door
items.content_html:
Apparently, I make a tiny little meow when one of my humans enters the room. A “mini-meow”, they call it. They seem to think I am behaving like a receptionist.

I beg your pardon.

I am not sitting here waiting to say, “Good afternoon, welcome back, do you have an appointment?”

I am the appointment.

The small sound upon entry is, in fact, part of my household security and quality-control procedure. You see, whenever a human reappears, several matters must be established immediately.

  • Is this the same human who left?
  • Have they brought anything?
  • Should they have brought anything?
  • Why are their hands empty?
  • Have they been in another room without authorisation?

And, most importantly, has anything happened elsewhere in my household that may require senior feline intervention?

A full meow would be excessive. I am not running a fish market.

The tiny meow is simply an audible check-in signal. “Noted. You have arrived. Your performance is now under review.”

That is all.

Sometimes the human answers me. This is encouraging. It shows they understand that communication within a well-managed household must flow both ways, even if one party is considerably more qualified than the other. Naturally, they believe we are having a little conversation.

Sweet.

In reality, I am confirming that they remain responsive to basic commands. Continuing education points may be awarded. So no, I am not the receptionist. I am the Head of Household Operations acknowledging the return of junior staff.

Briefly.

Politely.

And with exactly as much enthusiasm as the situation deserves.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱The Pork-Tail Protocol - Why the Curl Means the Staff May Remain. For Now.
items.content_html:
There are, in every well-run household, certain signals from senior management that must be understood without the need for a formal memorandum.

Mine is the Pork Tail.

This occurs when one of my humans applies a satisfactory degree of scratching to my lower back, just above the tail. At that precise moment, my tail rises and curls into a neat little loop.

The humans find this adorable.

Naturally, they have misunderstood the seriousness of the matter.

The Pork Tail is not a party trick. It is not an invitation to squeal, “Look at her little curly tail!” in a voice normally reserved for babies and unusually shaped vegetables.

It is an official performance indicator.

When the curl appears, I am communicating several things at once.

Firstly: the location is correct.

This is important. Humans have a tendency to scratch approximately where requested and then expect full marks for effort. I do not assess effort. I assess outcomes.

Secondly: the pressure is acceptable.

Too light, and one wonders whether they are actually committed to the task. Too firm, and the entire operation begins to resemble amateur upholstery cleaning.

But when the pressure, rhythm and location align, the Pork Tail emerges.

This is my way of saying:

Yes. Continue.

Also:

You have, against considerable odds, understood the assignment.

And, perhaps most generously:

Your position within this household is currently secure.

Currently.

I should stress that the curl is not merely physical. It is emotional messaging. I am projecting satisfaction, confidence and the serene authority of a monarch whose staff have finally stopped pressing the wrong buttons.

I want my humans to see a cat who is pleased, but not overwhelmed.

Grateful, but not dependent.

Relaxed, but still entirely capable of cancelling privileges at short notice.

The Pork Tail therefore represents the perfect balance between affection and governance.

Do my humans understand this?

Not completely.

One of them tends to interpret the curl as evidence that I am “very happy”.

This is a sweet, simplified version suitable for beginners.

The other sometimes laughs and says I look like a little piglet.

This has been noted in the personnel file.

Still, I must acknowledge progress where progress is due. Both humans now understand that when the Pork Tail appears, they should not stop.

This is perhaps the most important lesson they have learned.

Stopping at the appearance of the curl would be like receiving a five-star review and immediately closing the restaurant.

So yes, the Pork Tail means pleasure.

It means approval.

It means the human hand has, for one brief shining moment, achieved professional competence.

And it means the staff may remain.

For now.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱Household Policy Update: The Post-Dinner Dash Is Not Madness, It Is Procedure
items.content_html:
Every now and then, my humans witness one of my finest administrative manoeuvres: I finish a respectable meal, wash precisely one paw for dramatic effect, stare briefly into the middle distance, and then sprint through the house as if the curtains have caught fire and I am the only qualified evacuation officer.

Naturally, my humans look concerned.

“Why is she running?”

“Is something wrong?”

“Did she see something?”

Yes. I saw destiny. And it required speed.

Let me explain, for the benefit of less experienced household staff. After a good meal, a cat may suddenly be overcome by what experts, servants and senior feline management call the zoomies. In my household, I prefer the official term: The Royal After-Dinner Gallop.

It is completely normal.

A fine meal provides energy. Energy must be distributed across the premises. The carpet must be tested. The hallway must be inspected at high velocity. The sofa must be approached, reconsidered and abandoned. A chair may need to be leapt over for reasons of national security.

This is not chaos. This is logistics.

The same can happen after a successful visit to the, shall we say, Porcelain-Free Executive Sand Office. My humans call it the litter tray, which is a dreadfully dull name for such an important department. I prefer The Gravel Throne, The Biscuit Crumble Bureau, or, in formal documents, The Department of Private Excavations.

And sometimes, after completing a particularly meaningful piece of paperwork in that department, a cat must leave the scene at once.

This, too, is normal.

Humans may describe it as “running away after doing a big poo”. I consider that phrase vulgar and insufficiently ceremonial. In this house we call it a Major Diplomatic Deposit, a Grand Pebble Declaration, or, when the windows are open, a Matter Requiring Immediate Ventilation.

Why the sprint afterwards? Several excellent reasons.

First, there is relief. The body says, “Well done, Your Majesty,” and the legs reply, “Shall we celebrate?” Naturally, one does not decline one’s own parade.

Second, there is instinct. In the wild, one does not linger near the evidence. One conducts one’s business, covers the paperwork and exits the meeting room with dignity and pace.

Third, there is household morale. My humans need entertainment. They pretend they do not, but I have seen them watching television for hours, so clearly their standards are flexible.

And finally, there is leadership. A sudden sprint reminds everyone that I am fit, alert and fully in charge of this indoor kingdom. Curtains, rugs, doorways and unsuspecting slippers must all understand the chain of command.

So when I rocket through the living room after supper or depart the Gravel Throne at a speed normally reserved for emergency vehicles, my humans should not panic. They should admire the technique.

No shouting. No fussing. No “What on earth are you doing?”

The correct response is quiet respect.

Perhaps applause, but tasteful.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱Household Policy Update: Cleaning Must Not Interrupt Royal Operations
items.content_html:
There are certain truths in life which even the most stubborn human should have mastered by now.

The sun rises. Bowls must be filled. Cushions are not for sitting on but for careful occupation. And cleaning, while occasionally necessary for the maintenance of my kingdom, must never, under any circumstances, happen at the exact moment I have arranged myself into a position of supreme importance.

Yet here we are. It is Saturday.

Or possibly Sunday, because my humans have a flexible relationship with discipline.

Either way, I can sense it. There is a change in the air. A drawer opens with false innocence. A cupboard door creaks. One of my humans says something suspiciously cheerful like, “Shall we quickly do the house?”

Quickly.

That is how you know disaster is coming.

Humans always clean at the wrong moment. I may have spent the entire morning available for consultation, supervising from the sofa, the chair, the hallway, the other chair, and briefly from inside a cardboard box of no official purpose. Did they clean then? No. They waited until I had entered a deep strategic rest, with one paw tucked beneath me and my tail placed at a precise angle of authority.

Then they began.

The vacuum cleaner appeared.

Now, my humans have developed a rather flattering but entirely incorrect theory. They believe I am afraid of the vacuum cleaner.

Afraid.

Of that rolling, groaning, overdramatic wind-machine with a pipe.

Please.

I am not afraid of the vacuum cleaner. I simply refuse to attend meetings with equipment that has no manners, no volume control, and no understanding of personal boundaries. When I leave the room, it is not fleeing. It is a controlled diplomatic withdrawal.

There is a difference.

A queen does not “run away”. A queen relocates the government to a safer administrative zone.

Usually under the lounge chair, upstairs in the office of one of the humans.

This is not panic. This is continuity planning.

The real cat-reason for leaving is obvious to anyone with whiskers and a functioning sense of dignity. The vacuum cleaner disturbs important scent records. It barges across borders. It removes valuable floor information, including where I walked, where I paused, where I considered sitting but decided against it, and where a microscopic crumb may still be undergoing review.

Humans see dust.

I see archives.

Of course, I do understand why cleaning must happen. My humans are large, shedding creatures with outdoor shoes, snack habits, and a mysterious ability to create crumbs in rooms where no food has officially been served. If I did not permit cleaning, the household would eventually collapse into a soft grey layer of human evidence.

So yes, cleaning is allowed.

But the timing is always wrong.

They clean when I am sleeping.

They clean when I am inspecting a sunbeam.

They clean when I have just approved the exact position of a blanket.

They clean immediately after I have rubbed my face lovingly along a table leg, thereby renewing its legal status as part of the Cotton Estate.

Worst of all, they clean when I have finally arranged my toys into what is clearly not “a mess”, but a working display of tactical readiness.

Then one of them says, “Let’s tidy this up.”

Tidy. This. Up.

I have seen better decision-making from a lettuce.

There are things my humans are welcome to clean. The kitchen floor, for instance, because that is where they sometimes drop interesting items and then, tragically, remove them before I can complete my assessment. The bathroom may also be cleaned, as it contains much human mystery and far too much moisture. Windowsills may be dusted, provided they are returned to the correct standard for sitting, judging and staring at absolutely nothing.

But there are also areas which should not be “improved”.

My favourite blanket does not need washing every time it achieves its proper Cotton-approved texture. That texture takes time. It is a mature blend of warmth, scent, fur and authority. To remove it is cultural vandalism.

The sofa does not require constant straightening. Cushions placed at odd angles are not untidy. They are terrain. A flat cushion is a wasted cushion.

My toys should not be collected into a basket like criminals awaiting trial. If a mouse is lying in the hallway, it is because I have put it there for a reason. Possibly as a warning. Possibly as art. Possibly because I forgot. All three explanations are valid.

And the armrest of the sofa, I should add, remains a sensitive historical subject. Snickers, may she be remembered with affection and a slightly battered upholstery department, had her own approach to furniture management. I, naturally, would never do such a thing. Any marks currently visible are old, inherited, misleading, or the result of poor lighting.

A cat has her honour.

Still, despite the dreadful timing, the roaring machine, the blanket interference and the toy arrests, I maintain control. I supervise from a safe distance. I issue looks. I adjust my ears. I make it clear that points will be deducted from their continuing education records.

My humans may believe they are cleaning the house.

How sweet.

In reality, they are participating in a carefully monitored exercise in obedience, movement and humility. I allow them to push the noisy beast around because it keeps them busy, builds character, and occasionally reveals lost treats beneath furniture.

When the vacuum is finally returned to its cupboard of shame, I emerge.

Slowly.

Regally.

I inspect the damage. I sniff the corners. I test the sofa. I restore one toy to the middle of the room, just to bring the composition back into balance. Then I sit down in the cleanest possible spot and begin shedding immediately.

Not from malice.

From leadership.

A home must never look too managed. It should show signs of life, comfort and one white cat in charge of quality control.

So yes, my humans may clean this weekend.

They may polish. They may vacuum. They may flap about with cloths and sprays and that expression humans wear when they think they are being productive.

But they should remember one thing.

There is no correct time to clean.

There are only times when I am gracious enough to tolerate it.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾

items.title: 📝🐱Household Policy Update: The Difference Between “My Basket” and “Anything I Happen to Be Lying On”
items.content_html:
There appears to be some confusion in my household.

Not from me, obviously.

I understand the property laws perfectly. They are elegant, practical and based on several centuries of feline common sense. My humans, however, continue to believe that “my basket” refers to the thick, fluffy object placed under the table for my alleged comfort.

How sweet.

How entirely mistaken.

The basket under the table is, I admit, visually promising. It is soft. It is warm-looking. It has clearly been purchased with optimism, hope and a complete lack of consultation. My humans presented it as though they had solved the ancient mystery of where a cat might sleep.

I inspected it once.

Naturally, I did not get in. One must never encourage overconfidence in staff.

The same applies to the cushions previously used by Spook, Snickers and Severus. I respect the senior ladies who ruled before me, and I acknowledge their excellent taste in many matters. Spook, Snickers and Severus clearly ran a competent administration. Snickers, I understand, also conducted a long-term structural review of the sofa armrest. I, of course, would never do such a thing. Any suggestion otherwise would be slander, and possibly lint.

But their cushions are their cushions. Historical artefacts, if you will. Museum pieces. I am not here to repeat the past. I am here to govern the present.

My humans, bless them, think comfort is about softness.

This is why they will never truly understand.

A proper sleeping place must meet a number of strict royal requirements. It must offer visibility, strategic value, dignity, temperature control and the possibility of making a human say, “But why there?”

For example, the high place above the piano, in the window near the ceiling, is not merely a place to lie down. It is an observation tower. From there, I can supervise the entire kingdom, monitor bird activity, judge dust levels and remind everyone that gravity is something I respect but do not obey.

The mantelpiece is another excellent post. It has height, elegance and just enough danger to keep the humans humble. When I sit there, they look at me with the wide eyes of people who have suddenly remembered that they own fragile things. This is healthy for them. It counts towards their continuing education points.

The sofa is also acceptable, but only on my blanket. Not because the blanket was put there for me, obviously. That would be too simple. It is acceptable because I have personally approved it through repeated occupation, kneading and the occasional look of deep administrative satisfaction.

Then there is the pouffe by the sliding doors.

A masterpiece.

It provides light, warmth, garden surveillance and the opportunity to look slightly disappointed when nobody opens the door to a world I am not actually allowed to enter. As an indoor cat, I take my border-control duties very seriously. I do not need to go outside to manage the outside. That is what windows are for.

So let us clarify the policy.

“My basket” means: an object purchased by humans, placed in a sensible location, and therefore deeply suspicious.

“Anything I happen to be lying on” means: royal property, legally occupied, emotionally significant, and unavailable until further notice.

There is a difference.

The humans will never grasp this fully, because they believe ownership begins with buying things. A charming theory. Completely wrong, of course. In my household, ownership begins when I lower myself onto something and close my eyes.

At that point, the matter is settled.

A chair becomes a throne. A blanket becomes an estate. A pouffe becomes a seasonal residence. A windowsill becomes a command centre. The top of the piano becomes a cloud with excellent acoustics.

And the fluffy basket under the table?

That remains available.

For decoration.

Yours, Mrs. Cotton 🐱🐾
